setting.tagline: A war over the nature of truth, fought with salt and brine on the corpse of a god, with a clock everyone can hear.
setting.premise: When the leviathan-deity Veyl was slain in the deep past, it did not bleed — it wept, and its grief filled the basin of the world to become the Litany Sea, an ocean of brine in which every drop held a remembered moment. Now the Sea is dying: the rust-red sun has not set in living memory, and the brine is evaporating, receding thigh-deep then ankle-deep then gone, crystallizing as it goes into salt-glass that fossilizes real history — each crystal a moment you can re-live, sell, edit, set forever, or shatter so that it never happened at all. Across this drying flat wade the memory-archivists, rival orders who have realized that whichever version of the past is still crystallized when the last pool dries will become the only past there ever was. They fight not for ground or for kills but for custody of specific, fragile, irreplaceable crystals — and the central agony of every battle is seizing or guarding the thing you came for without shattering it in the crossfire. The whole flat is alive and audibly counting down: pools crystallize, crystals ring and crack, brine floods and recedes turn over turn, while the salt-bodied dead of forgotten moments rise and re-rise wherever the tide abandons them. The Sea has perhaps a single long afternoon left, and it is tolling.
setting.theTwist: The leviathan-deity Veyl is not dead — it is grieving, and the Litany Sea is not its corpse but its open, weeping wound, still dreaming. Every crystal is a tear it has not finished crying, and the "history" the archivists fight to fix or erase is in fact Veyl actively re-remembering its own life as it dies, which is why the salt-dead keep rising: they are the god flinching at moments it cannot let go. The brine is not evaporating from heat — it is being wept out, and when the last pool dries, Veyl will have finished the thought. The faction whose version of the past has crystallized at that instant does not "win" the map; it authors the single memory the god carries into death, and thereby becomes the only true history of the world. The archivists believe they are scavengers looting a divine cadaver. They are, in truth, the competing voices inside a dying mind's last sentence — and the loser's past does not merely fail to score, it ceases ever to have happened.

terminology.meaning: The shared, audible countdown of the receding brine — measured in 'tides' (game rounds). Every faction reads the same Toll; when it strikes dry, the table's crystallized state becomes the verdict and the game ends.
A crystallized memory. A single fossilized moment of real history, fragile and irreplaceable. A named, lore-bearing objective crystal is called a Litany; common scoring crystals are just salt-glass.

The two states of any board zone. Brine-deep zones are flooded and movement-slowing but protect crystals from shattering; Dry zones are fast and lethal — exposed crystals there can be shattered by stray fire.
The act of making a crystal permanent — 'setting' a memory so it can never be edited, sold, or shattered for the rest of the game. The Mnemarchs' sacred verb and core win path.
When the receding tide tries to erase a Reliquia, the god's grief sometimes re-remembers it, returning the model to play. The Sediment's resource and the engine of the swarm.

The end-state epistemological scoring: which faction's ontology of the past — fixed, erased, sold, or freed — controls the most crystallized history when the Sea dries. Not body count, not control points: which version of the truth survived.

In-world slang for an archivist who has re-lived too many crystals and can no longer tell their own memories from the Sea's. The smell of iodine on the flat means a fresh memory is crystallizing nearby.

timeline.event: The leviathan-deity Veyl is mortally wronged and weeps without ceasing. Its grief floods the basin of the world, and the Litany Sea is born — an ocean in which every moment of all history is suspended, intact, in solution.

The rust-red sun rises and never sets. The brine begins, almost imperceptibly, to recede. The first salt-glass forms at the shrinking margins, and a wading hermit re-lives a crystal — discovering that the past can be touched, held, and changed.

Four orders crystallize around four mutually exclusive answers to one question: what is the past FOR? The Mnemarchs vow to fix it, the Ash Iconoclasts to erase it, the Brine-Factors to sell it, the Sediment to free it. The Custody Wars begin.

timeline.when: The Shattering of the Concord Litany
timeline.event: A truce-treaty crystal — the one memory all four factions had agreed to protect — is shattered in crossfire during a three-way raid. The moment of the peace is unmade; no one now remembers agreeing to it. Total war becomes the only history.

The recession accelerates from a slow creep to an audible, board-wide countdown. Pools that took ages to dry now dry within a single engagement. The salt-dead begin rising faster than the tide can erase them. The present day: the Sea has one long afternoon left.

timeline.when: The Last Pool (the moment of play)
timeline.event: Every battle is now fought in the final tides of the Long Toll. When the last brine dries, Veyl finishes its dying thought — and whichever version of the past is set in salt-glass at that instant becomes the only past that ever was.

worldMechanics.name: The Long Toll (the living, audible clock)
worldMechanics.concept: The receding brine is a shared doomsday clock every faction reads identically. The Sea is genuinely alive during play: each round the tide marker advances one step on a fixed track audible as the 'Toll,' and the entire board physically transforms — Brine-deep zones recede to Dry, exposing crystals; new pools never return. Time is not abstract; it is the water leaving the table.
worldMechanics.ruleHook: Use a physical Tide Track of fixed length (e.g. 6 tides). At the start of every round, advance the Tide marker one notch — this is mandatory, unskippable, and identical for all players (no faction speeds or slows the base Toll). Each notch flips a pre-defined band of board zones from Brine-deep to Dry via a double-sided terrain overlay (wet side up / dry side up). BINARY, instant, visible: a zone is wet or dry, never 'partially.' A crystal in a Dry zone is now Exposed (shatter-eligible). When the marker reaches the final notch, the Toll strikes Dry: the game ends immediately and the Verdict is scored. No turn counting in your head — the water tells you how long is left.

worldMechanics.name: Custody & Collateral (capture WITHOUT breaking)
worldMechanics.concept: Crystals are fragile, irreplaceable, lore-bearing OBJECTS, not abstract tokens. The core tension is seizing or protecting a specific thing without shattering it in the crossfire — collateral damage as the central dilemma. You cannot win by destroying the board; you win by having intact, controlled history when the Sea dries.
worldMechanics.ruleHook: Crystals are physical models with a CUSTODY state: Loose, Held (a model in base contact controls it), or Set (permanent). Any time an attack's shots miss a target in or adjacent to an Exposed crystal's zone, the attacker rolls the misses against the crystal: each natural 6 (Sixes philosophy — no modifiers, just raw dice) is a Shatter hit; enough Shatters and the crystal is destroyed and removed — it never happened, and nobody scores it. BINARY decision every activation: take the risky shot near the prize, or hold fire. Carrying a crystal is an IGNORE-X tradeoff — a model carrying a Litany cannot Run and cannot shoot, trading mobility/firepower for custody. Brine-deep zones AUTO-PASS the shatter check (water cushions the glass); the instant a zone goes Dry on the Toll, that protection is gone. The board state, not a stat line, tells you what is safe to shoot near.

worldMechanics.name: The Dreaming Grief (re-dreaming & board corruption)
worldMechanics.concept: Veyl's grief still dreams, and the salt-dead — Reliquiae, ghosts who exist only while their crystal stays solid — are the crisis given a face. The more the board dries and the more crystals shatter, the more the god flinches and re-remembers its dead, so the horde scales with the very corruption the other factions cause. Erasure becomes a resource rather than only a loss.
worldMechanics.ruleHook: Maintain a single visible Grief pool that gains a token every time ANY crystal shatters or ANY zone flips to Dry (board-wide, all factions trigger it — it ties to visible board state, not bookkeeping). Reliquiae are expendable horde models with a binary existence clause: a Reliquia removed as a casualty is set aside, not destroyed. At the start of each round, spend Grief tokens to Re-dream set-aside Reliquiae back onto the board in any Dry zone — AUTO-RETURN, no roll. This makes the swarm an engine that grows precisely as the table degrades: the more violence the other three factions do, the larger the horde re-dreams. A Reliquia standing in a Brine-deep zone when it recedes to Dry is NOT erased; one the tide passes over twice IS — IGNORE only while wet, gone when dry, a visible on/off tied to the terrain overlay.

factions.name: The Mnemarchs (Order of the Set Hour)
factions.identity: Cathedral-archivists in salt-stiffened vestments who believe the past is sacred and must be FIXED — made permanent, true, and untouchable. They do not loot history; they enshrine it. To set a memory in salt-glass forever, exactly as it happened, is their highest sacrament and their win condition.
factions.pillar: PRESERVATION / LOCK-DOWN — the only faction that can permanently Set crystals, removing them from every other faction's reach. They win by sanctifying truth, not by quantity.
factions.playstyle: Elite / attrition / defensive zone-holding. Few, expensive, durable models that bunker around a Litany and grind out the clock, daring you to come take an objective you cannot safely shoot near.
factions.colorMotif: Bone-white and verdigris bronze — bleached vestments, oxidized reliquary fittings, salt-rimed gold.

factions.name: The Ash Iconoclasts (the Shattering)
factions.identity: Zealot-purgers who hold that the past is a wound and the only mercy is to erase it. Every crystal is a lie that imprisons; they came to break all of it so the god can finally stop remembering. They refuse, on principle, to score history — they exist to deny it to everyone else.
factions.pillar: DENIAL / NEGATION — the anti-scoring faction. They cannot and will not 'win the past'; they win by ensuring NO ontology survives intact, shattering Litanies the others die to protect. The board-cleansing zealot archetype imported whole.
factions.playstyle: Aggressive firepower / glass-cannon shock. Fragile, hard-hitting shatter-specialists who weaponize collateral, deliberately fighting in Dry zones to expose and break crystals — turning the central 'don't break the prize' tension against everyone.
factions.colorMotif: Charcoal and ember-orange — scorched grey robes, burnt-iodine smoke, glowing crack-lines like cooling slag.

factions.name: The Brine-Factors (the Salt Exchange)
factions.identity: Mercantile salvagers and memory-brokers who see the dying Sea as the final liquidation sale of all history. The past is inventory: re-live it, edit it for a buyer, and above all SELL it. Truth is whatever the highest bid says it is, and they intend to cash out before the Toll strikes dry.
factions.pillar: EXTRACTION / ECONOMY — the resource-conversion faction. They EDIT crystals (changing what a memory scores as) and trade them, generating an in-game currency that fuels reinforcements and bribes. They win by controlling the market of the past, not its truth.
factions.playstyle: Mobility / trickery / tempo. Fast, light, opportunistic crews of skiff-riders and cutpurses who snatch crystals, edit them mid-game, and redeploy — never holding ground, always working the angles.
factions.colorMotif: Brass and deep teal — patinaed brass scales, ledger-ink teal sashes, glittering coin-cut salt.

factions.name: The Sediment (the Re-Dreaming)
factions.identity: The crisis given a face: the salt-bodied Reliquiae and the grief-touched hierophants who shepherd them, who believe the past must be FREED — let the god finish weeping, let every fixed moment dissolve back into the Sea. They embrace erasure as liberation and grow stronger the more the board dies.
factions.pillar: CORRUPTION-SCALING SWARM — the only faction that turns the board's decay into fuel, re-dreaming expendable models from the Grief pool. They want maximum entropy: floods, shatters, and drying all feed them. The fourth ontology that completes the asymmetry.
factions.playstyle: Horde / expendable attrition / board control. Many cheap, returning models that drown objectives in numbers, re-dreaming as fast as they fall, weaponizing the receding tide and rising Grief that erodes everyone else.
factions.colorMotif: Pale salt-grey and bruise-violet — translucent crystalline flesh, deep-water violet shadow, iridescent brine-sheen.

winner.mergedConcept: A skirmish game of warring memory-archivists fighting over a dying god's drying tears. The world is the Litany Sea — a vast evaporating salt flat that was once an ocean of a slain leviathan-deity's grief. As the brine recedes it crystallizes around real moments of history: every salt crystal is a fossilized memory you can re-live, sell, edit, set forever, or shatter so it never happened. From CRISTALLO comes the game's sharpest tactical engine and its emotional teeth: memory-crystals are not abstract tokens but fragile, irreplaceable, lore-bearing OBJECTS, so the central tension becomes seizing or protecting specific things WITHOUT breaking them in the crossfire — collateral damage as the core dilemma, and grief itself as a faction motive. From THE LONG TOLL / TINNITUS comes the doomsday-clock-as-resource discipline: the receding brine is an audible, visible countdown every faction reads identically, and the battlefield is genuinely ALIVE and degrading during play — pools crystallize, crystals shatter, brine floods and recedes turn over turn, so terrain manipulation becomes each faction's native verb rather than a static map. From THE LONG SLEEP comes the deepened metaphysics and the swarm archetype that completes the asymmetry quartet: the leviathan-deity's grief still "dreams," and the Reliquiae (salt-bodied memory-ghosts who exist only while their crystal stays solid) are reframed as the crisis given a face — expendable, re-dreaming horde models that the receding tide keeps trying to erase. The result keeps Salt-Glass Litany's killer differentiator intact — the win condition is an epistemological VERDICT (which version of the past has crystallized when the table dries) rather than body count or control points — while borrowing the most table-legible, mechanically generative ideas from its rivals. Four factions hold mutually exclusive ontologies of the past (fix it, erase it, sell it, free it), so the lore IS the rules: bone-white deserts under a rust-red sun, figures wading thigh-deep in mirror-still brine, the constant tinkle of crystals and the smell of iodine. A war over the nature of truth, fought with salt and brine on the corpse of a god, with a clock everyone can hear.
graftedIdeas: From CRISTALLO: memory-crystals as fragile, irreplaceable, capture-WITHOUT-breaking OBJECTS — making collateral damage and 'don't shatter the prize in the crossfire' the central tactical tension, and importing the Ash Iconoclasts' shatter-everything zealot as a denial archetype that refuses to score.

From THE LONG TOLL / TINNITUS: the audible, shared doomsday clock as a true game resource and pacing mechanism — every faction reads the same receding-brine timer, and the battlefield physically transforms (crystallize / shatter / flood / recede) DURING play, turning terrain manipulation into each faction's signature verb.

From THE LONG SLEEP / 'Sediment': the deeper leviathan-deity cosmology (the god's grief still dreams) plus the re-dreaming expendable swarm — recasting the Reliquiae as a horde-of-the-crisis-given-a-face that scales with board corruption and embraces erasure as a resource, rounding out the four-pillar asymmetry.
winner.rationale: Salt-Glass Litany scores highest on the two criteria that matter most for a shippable skirmish game: tabletop suitability and faction-asymmetry. Its objective interactions (harvest / set / shatter / un-crystallize) are concrete physical verbs that map directly onto miniature actions and a real board, and its four factions hold genuinely MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE win-conditions (fix vs erase vs sell vs free the past) rather than the same goal with different flavor — the cleanest asymmetry of any pitch, because each faction can WIN while the others actively cannot. Its 'epistemological verdict' victory condition is the single most ownable idea across all five pitches and is impossible to confuse with anything on a shelf. The three sound-based pitches (Long Toll, Tinnitus, Long Sleep) are dazzling but share a weakness: 'sound as terrain' is abstract and hard to represent with physical minis and tokens (where does a 'standing wave' sit on the table? how do players track pitch?), and Long Toll vs Tinnitus are near-duplicates of each other, which actually lowers each one's originality in context. Cristallo is the strongest rival — historically grounded, instantly explainable, with the best object-capture tension — but its real-Venice setting caps its originality ceiling and its all-human, small-scale premise limits visual faction variety. Salt-Glass Litany is the best SPINE because it already fuses Cristallo's fragile-object tension and the sound-pitches' degrading-living-terrain and doomsday-clock into a setting that is weird, emotionally legible, and free of every fantasy/sci-fi cliché. Grafting Cristallo's capture-without-breaking dilemma, the Toll/Tinnitus living-clock-and-terrain, and Long Sleep's deity cosmology + re-dreaming swarm patches its only soft spots (somewhat thin moment-to-moment tactical engine and an under-defined fourth faction) without diluting its core identity.

scores.title: THE LONG SLEEP / "Sediment"
scores.note: Originality 9 (collapsing battlefield+antagonist+prize into one living god is genuinely fresh; palliative-care-for-a-god framing is striking). Coherence 8 (the four stances toward a waking god are tight and well-differentiated). Tabletop suitability 6 (mutating terrain and dream-blooms are evocative but bookkeeping-heavy and hard to render with static minis; 'rules shift as terrain dreams' risks fiddly tracking). Faction-asymmetry 9 (Soporifists/Choir/Renderworks/Molt map cleanly onto control/tempo/economy/swarm and want different relationships to the crisis). Strong concept; the body-horror swarm and dream-bloom economy are the most graftable parts.

scores.title: THE LONG TOLL
scores.note: Originality 8 (sound-as-load-bearing-matter and pitch-as-resource is vivid). Coherence 8 (tuners/harvesters/silencers/riders are a clean four-verb set: harden/shatter/rot/exploit). Tabletop suitability 6 (a 'climbable, flattening sound' is beautiful but abstract to represent physically; the dropping-pitch clock is a strong shared mechanic). Faction-asymmetry 7 (good, but Riders 'exploit others' terrain changes' is a parasitic playstyle that can feel reactive/unsatisfying solo). Hurt in context by near-identity with Tinnitus; the audible doomsday clock is its best graftable contribution.

scores.title: CRISTALLO: The Breathing Glass of Venice
scores.note: Originality 8 (one rigorous twist on real history; loses a point because the setting itself is a known place rather than an invented cosmology). Coherence 10 (the single rule — glass records breath — generates the entire economy, politics, and faction set with zero handwaving; the tightest internal logic of all five). Tabletop suitability 9 (fragile irreplaceable OBJECTS you must capture without breaking is a superb, instantly-teachable tactical loop; small surgical skirmishes suit minis perfectly). Faction-asymmetry 6 (Maestri/Sealed Mouth/Drowned/Cenere are well-drawn but all human and several share 'control the glass' goals; visual variety is limited). The strongest rival and the richest donor of mechanics.

scores.title: TINNITUS: Wars of the Last Sound
scores.note: Originality 8 (ringing-ears-as-cosmology is a bold elevation of a mundane sensation). Coherence 8 (Resonance = power AND exposure is an elegant risk economy; four endings/factions are coherent). Tabletop suitability 5 (the most abstract of all — moving across 'volume and pitch' rather than ground is conceptually thrilling but the hardest to physically lay out and track; Loud/Quiet/Cancellation/Standing-Wave zones need heavy markers). Faction-asymmetry 8 (Choir/Mute/Feedback/Echobound are distinct: formation-buff/denial/burst/recursion). Largely redundant with The Long Toll, which drags its in-context originality down.

scores.title: SALT-GLASS LITANY
scores.note: Originality 9 (memory-as-terrain with an epistemological-verdict win condition is the most ownable single idea in the set; no orcs/empires/spaceships/chosen-ones). Coherence 9 (drying-brine clock + crystals-as-fossilized-memory + four ontologies of the past all interlock cleanly). Tabletop suitability 9 (harvest/set/shatter/dissolve are concrete physical verbs on real objects; the drying-table is a built-in pacing clock; small warbands suit skirmish). Faction-asymmetry 10 (the only pitch where factions have MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE victory conditions — fix vs erase vs sell vs free — so the asymmetry is structural, not cosmetic). Chosen as the spine: highest weighted total and the best foundation to absorb the others' best mechanics.

universalKeywords.keyword: Crystal States: Loose / Held / Set / Exposed
universalKeywords.text: The four readable states of a salt-glass crystal, shown by markers on the board. LOOSE: uncontested, in no model's base contact. HELD: a model is in base contact and controls it. SET: permanently sealed (Mnemarchs only) — can never be Held, edited, sold, shattered, moved, or re-dreamed again. EXPOSED: the crystal sits in a Dry zone with no friendly model cushioning it, making it eligible to be Shattered or targeted by a Breaking Volley. State is always determined by visible board position, never by hidden tracking.

universalKeywords.keyword: Zone States: Brine-deep / Dry, and the Toll
universalKeywords.text: Every objective zone is either BRINE-DEEP (wet) or DRY. The TOLL (also called the Long Toll) is the receding-tide clock: at a fixed point each round the tide advances and one or more Brine-deep zones flip to Dry, permanently for that strike. Wet zones cushion crystals (a crystal in a Brine-deep zone auto-passes any Shatter check); Dry zones expose them. Many signature rules are gated on wet-vs-dry, so the Toll is the master tempo engine all four factions race against. Flipping a zone Dry is a visible, table-wide trigger that feeds the Sediment's Grief pool.

The single destruction mechanic for crystals. A Shatter hit is normally scored only on a natural 6 by stray collateral; some rules lower the threshold (Iconoclasts: natural 5-6 on a Breaking Volley) or guarantee it. A crystal in a Brine-deep zone AUTO-PASSES the Shatter check for every faction without rolling — water cannot be shattered. Each crystal that shatters, regardless of whose, automatically adds 1 token to the Sediment Grief pool. Binary on a single die: either it breaks or it does not, no accumulated modifiers.

Certain permanent actions — chiefly the Set Hour — require two Witness models present. A unit with the Witness keyword (e.g. a Lector of the Permitted Truth, or the Two Witnesses character) counts as one of the required two. Witnessing is a binary presence check tied to model position, not a modifier; either the second Witness is in range or the action cannot be declared.

Movement-restriction keywords on the slow, ritual-bound forces (the Mnemarchs carry both on nearly every unit). CANNOT RUN: the model may never take the Run action, capping its move at its base distance — it cannot rush objectives, it must be deployed where it intends to stand. SALT-STIFFENED: the model is treated as a fixed, durable fixture; it cannot be pushed, dragged, or repositioned by enemy effects. Both are binary on/off, instantly read from the model's keyword line.

A guarding effect: a model with this keyword in base contact with a crystal extends the wet-zone AUTO-PASS Shatter protection to that crystal even in a Dry zone, as long as the model stands and is not removed. Binary protection tied to a single visible model in base contact — remove or move the guardian and the cushion is gone instantly. Bridges the Mnemarchs' Verdigris Wardens and the crystal they protect.

The Brine-Factors' physical resource pool, shown as salt tokens on the board rather than tracked on paper. Earned by liquidating crystals into Hold; spent the instant a trigger fires (even during an opponent's activation) to pay for reinforcements, edits, and bribes. A faction at zero Coin is 'liquidated' and suffers a binary penalty. Coin is never a numeric modifier to a roll — it is a yes/no fuel that either is or is not available to switch a binary effect on.

The Sediment's shared resource, filled automatically by table-wide degradation: +1 per crystal shattered (anyone's) and +1 per zone that flips Dry on the Toll. Spent 1-for-1 at the start of a round to AUTO-RETURN dead Reliquiae to the board — no roll, no scatter. Visible token pool, instant to apply, and explicitly tied to board state the whole table can see, so opponents always know how big the next re-dream can be.

A crystal-alteration action shared by the Brine-Factors (paid in Coin) and referenced by the Iodine Cartel's forgers. Editing changes which faction's ontology a Loose or Held crystal will count for at the Verdict, or swaps a real crystal for a counterfeit. Binary state-swap on the crystal marker, instant, board-visible — it does not nudge a number, it flips ownership/authenticity outright. Cannot be performed on a Set crystal.

A denial action carried by several Sediment units and conceptually opposed to the Mnemarch Set Hour: a Reliquia in base contact with a crystal in a Brine-deep zone can keep it wet/submerged, preventing it from being Exposed, Shattered, or Set. Binary protection tied to the model's presence and the zone being wet; ends the instant the model dies or the Toll dries the zone.

The end-of-game scoring resolution. Each faction counts its own ontology differently: Mnemarchs count Set crystals only; Brine-Factors count crystals in Hold; Sediment count surviving Reliquiae/edited crystals; Iconoclasts score by silence (crystals shattered / denied). Because each faction scores a different verb on the same crystal, the Verdict is read once from the visible board, not from cumulative bonuses.

distinctiveness.faction: The Mnemarchs (Order of the Set Hour)
distinctiveness.signatureMechanic: The Set Hour — the ONLY way in the game to make a crystal permanent. A binary, irreversible seal that can be performed only on a crystal in a Brine-deep (wet) zone, with two Witnesses. Once Set, the crystal can never be touched by anyone (including the Mnemarchs) and counts for their Verdict for the rest of the game. They win by how many they Set before the water leaves, not by how many they hold.
distinctiveness.playstyle: Slow, immovable, anvil-and-ritual control. Nearly every unit Cannot Run and is Salt-Stiffened, so the Mnemarchs cannot chase — they pick a wet zone, plant a bastion (Verdigris Wardens carrying Cushion of the Brine), bring Witnesses and the Sealing Choir, and try to complete the Set ritual before the Toll dries the ground out from under them. The core tension is timing: Set too early and you waste sacraments on uncontested crystals; wait for safety and the tide may strip the wet zone first. Tempo-poor but produces the only truly unkillable scoring on the table.

distinctiveness.signatureMechanic: Collateral Is the Point / Breaking Volley — uniquely, they aim AT the crystal on purpose. On a declared Breaking Volley against an enemy in/adjacent to an Exposed crystal, EVERY die (hits and misses) is also rolled against the crystal, and a natural 5 or 6 Shatters it (everyone else needs a 6, and only on stray dice). They are the only faction whose power grows by destroying history rather than guarding it.
distinctiveness.playstyle: Hyper-aggressive, fragile, board-burning glass cannons. Cheap expendable bodies (Slag-Pick Penitents at 8 pts), We Keep No Relics and Faith Without Memory mean they never hold or score crystals the normal way — they advance the Scour and force impossible choices: the enemy guarding an Exposed prize must either stand in front of the Breaking Volley (and die) or step away (and let the crystal shatter). They cannot work wet zones (water auto-passes), so they live and die on punishing whatever the Toll dries out. Tempo-rich, durability-poor.

distinctiveness.signatureMechanic: The Open Ledger — they do not score by holding crystals, they score by SELLING them. Disengaging a Factor from a Loose/Held crystal lifts it off the board into the Hold (untouchable, scoring) and earns 1 Coin; Coin is the fuel for every other Factor rule and can be spent during anyone's activation. A crystal in Hold scores but does nothing further, and at zero Coin you are 'liquidated' — any crystal taken into Hold must be sold straight back to the table.
distinctiveness.playstyle: Mobile, opportunistic, economic tempo. Fast cheap snatchers (Cutpurses, Reach-Runners, Skiff-Reach Corsairs) dart in, liquidate contested crystals, and bank Coin to bribe, edit, and reinforce reactively. The constant brutal decision is liquidity vs. presence: a sold crystal is safe and counts but is off the board doing nothing, and you can never sit still on your wealth — spend to zero and you collapse. They reward kinetic, never-moored play and out-tempo opponents by removing the prize before anyone can break or seal it.

distinctiveness.signatureMechanic: The Re-Dreaming — they never lose a model, they send it back. Casualties go to a Re-Dreaming pile; at the start of each round (after the Toll) Grief tokens are spent 1-for-1 to AUTO-RETURN them to any Dry zone, no roll, no scatter. The Grief pool fills from the whole table's violence (every shatter, every drying zone), so the more the board degrades the bigger the swarm re-dreams. The only hard limit: a Reliquia the receding brine passes over twice is erased for good.
distinctiveness.playstyle: Attritional swarm that feeds on the game's own decay. Dirt-cheap expendable bodies (Wadeling Drift at 6 pts, Murmur-Host at 7) are spent like water because the drying board pays them back. They smother objectives, Drown The Prize to deny Sets, and grow stronger precisely when opponents are most active — Iconoclast shatters and Mnemarch crystal-fights both refill Grief. The core skill is managing the two-tide erasure clock so the recursion engine never actually empties. Durability-rich through recursion, individually disposable.

rivalries.between: The Mnemarchs vs. The Ash Iconoclasts
rivalries.nature: The defining ideological war of the setting: permanence against erasure. The Mnemarchs exist to Set the past forever; the Iconoclasts exist to point the gun at history and Shatter it on purpose. Mechanically they are mirror enemies — the Set Hour can only happen in wet zones (where Iconoclast volleys auto-fail), while the Breaking Volley can only land in Dry zones (where Mnemarch crystals are Exposed). They fight a tug-of-war across the receding tideline: whoever owns the moment a zone flips owns whether that crystal is sealed forever or silenced forever.

A grudge of value versus reverence. To the Factors a crystal is inventory to be liquidated and sold; to the Mnemarchs it is a holy moment to be sealed beyond all commerce. The Set Hour is the one act that makes a crystal worthless to the Factors — Set crystals can never be sold, edited, or taken into Hold. So Factors race to liquidate contested crystals OFF the board before the Sealing Choir can complete its ritual, while Mnemarchs see every sale as a sacrilege that turns memory into a salt-token. Pure tempo rivalry: snatch-and-sell against plant-and-seal.

rivalries.between: The Ash Iconoclasts vs. The Sediment
rivalries.nature: A tragic symbiosis turned hatred. The Iconoclasts despise the Sediment because nothing the Scour destroys truly dies — every crystal the Iconoclasts shatter feeds the Grief pool and re-dreams the very swarm that smothers them. The Sediment, in turn, are drawn to the Iconoclasts' wake like undertow to a wreck, growing fattest exactly where the Shattering has been busiest. The Iconoclasts want silence; the Sediment turn that silence into more bodies. Each makes the other stronger, and both resent it.

Two rival answers to 'a crystal is never gone.' The Factors take a crystal OFF the table into the Hold where no one can touch it — past as locked asset. The Sediment keep the past circulating, re-dreaming the drowned back onto the board — past as endless tide. They clash over the same Loose crystals in the same Dry zones: the Factor wants to liquidate it into untouchable Coin; the Sediment wants to Drown it, deny the sale, and let the receding water keep it in play. Hoarding against recurrence.

council.balanceNotes:
DESIGN-PHILOSOPHY COMPLIANCE: All four signature rules pass the SIXES test — they are BINARY/IGNORE-X/AUTO effects, not modifier soup. Set Hour = irreversible binary flag. Breaking Volley = changes the Shatter threshold to a fixed natural 5-6 and adds EXTRA DICE (all dice, not just 6s) rather than stacking +1s. Open Ledger = remove-from-board state change plus a yes/no Coin fuel. Re-Dreaming = AUTO-RETURN with no roll and no scatter. None resolve to 'a number on the way to the same result.' The Brine wet-zone protection is a clean AUTO-PASS (no save modifier), and the Bronze Vigil's 'auto-pass first failed save while still' is IGNORE-X, both compliant. Recommend auditing any future stat-line bonuses to keep them as extra dice / re-rolls / ignore-X only.

WET-vs-DRY IS THE MASTER BALANCER. The Toll is the single lever that keeps all four in check: Mnemarchs and Sediment want wetness (Set requires wet; Drown requires wet), Iconoclasts and Factors thrive on dry (Breaking Volley needs Exposed/Dry; Factors sell into Dry zones, liquidate freely). As the game progresses and zones flip Dry, the power axis naturally tilts from the sealers/drowners toward the breakers/sellers — a built-in late-game swing. WATCH: if the Toll table dries zones too fast, Mnemarchs become unable to Set at all (they have no Run, no catch-up tempo) and the Sediment lose their wet anchors; if too slow, Iconoclasts and Factors are starved of targets. The Toll schedule should be the primary tuning knob, tested across maps, before touching unit points.

TEMPO vs DURABILITY MATRIX is intentionally orthogonal and looks healthy: Mnemarchs (tempo-poor, permanence-rich), Iconoclasts (tempo-rich, durability-poor), Factors (tempo-rich via cheap movers, fragile economy), Sediment (recursion-durable, individually disposable). No two share both axes, so no faction is strictly dominant.

SPECIFIC WATCH-LIST: (1) Sediment Grief feedback loop — Grief fills from EVERYONE's violence, so in a 1v1 vs Iconoclasts the swarm could spiral; the two-tide erasure clock is the only brake. Verify on tabletop that erasure actually outpaces re-dream in a heavy-shatter game, or the Iconoclast matchup is unwinnable for the breaker. (2) Mnemarch counterplay — because Set is irreversible and Cannot-Run makes them immobile, opponents need reliable ways to contest the WET zone BEFORE the Set lands (Sediment Drown, Factor liquidate, Iconoclast cannot help here since water auto-passes). Confirm at least two factions can deny a Set in progress, or Mnemarchs become a non-interactive turtle. (3) Factor 'liquidated at zero Coin' — make sure the forced sell-back is punishing enough that hoarding-then-dumping isn't optimal; the rule should bite, not be a minor speed bump. (4) Pilgrim-Bearers and Hauler-Sledge create off-board scoring custody — double-check these cannot stack with Hold/Set to double-count the same crystal at the Verdict.

POINTS SANITY: Chaff floor is well-spread (Sediment Wadeling 6 / Murmur-Host 7, Iconoclast Slag-Pick 8, Sediment Stranded 9, Factor/Mnemarch ~10) which correctly makes the recursion and swarm factions the cheapest-bodied. Command monsters cluster 22-32. Costs look internally consistent; no obvious outlier, but the Iconoclast Glass-Wraith Detonator (13 pts, guaranteed shatter) is the highest-variance unit on the table and should be playtested against Set/Cushion to ensure a single 13-pt model can't reliably erase a 30-pt guarded objective for free."

factions.name: The Mnemarchs (Order of the Set Hour)
factions.battleCry: "What was, shall be. We do not remember it — we make it so."

lore.origin: The Mnemarchs began with a single wading hermit at the First Recession — the one who first re-lived a crystal and learned the past could be touched. But where others felt the thrill of a thing that could be changed, this hermit, an old reliquary-keeper named Osseil the Stilled, felt only horror: if the past can be edited, then nothing is true, and a world with no fixed truth is a world already dead. Osseil knelt in the shrinking margin and did the opposite of editing — they pressed both palms to a crystallizing tear and willed it to stay exactly as it was, forever, refusing the temptation to make it better. The crystal Set. It rang once, clear, and could never again be altered, sold, or broken. Osseil wept, because they understood they had just performed the only mercy the dying Sea could be given, and the only blasphemy: to seal a single moment of a god's grief and call it scripture. From that first Set Hour grew the Order — those who came to the flat not to take history but to ordain it.
lore.culture: Mnemarch culture is liturgical, slow, and obsessively rigorous. They wear salt-stiffened vestments that crust harder with every crystal they Set, so that a senior archivist can barely move — rigidity is rank, and a fully-Set elder is a walking reliquary who has not bent at the waist in years. They speak in 'attestations': nothing is true until two witnesses have re-lived a crystal and sworn it matches, word for word, breath for breath. To them, editing is heresy and selling is desecration, but the deepest sin is the Iconoclast's — to unmake a moment is to murder a piece of the divine. They keep the Concord Litany's shattering as their original wound and recite the names of moments that 'never happened' as a funeral rite, mourning histories no one else can even remember losing. They do not loot. They genuflect, attest, and Set. They believe they are the Sea's confessors, taking down its last words exactly, so that when Veyl dies it dies remembered truly rather than flattered, sold, or silenced.
lore.whyTheyFight: The Mnemarchs fight because the Verdict is coming and they alone believe the past has intrinsic worth that must not be touched. If the Brine-Factors win, the god's last memory will be a forgery edited to suit a buyer. If the Ash Iconoclasts win, there will be no last memory at all — the god dies mid-sentence, erased. If the Sediment wins, every fixed truth dissolves and nothing was ever real. The Mnemarchs cannot abide any of these. They fight to Set the true moments before the Toll strikes dry, so that Veyl carries into death an honest account of its own life — neither flattered nor forgotten. They do not want to win the most history. They want the right history to survive untouched, and they will bunker around a single sacred Litany and grind out the entire clock to keep one true thing safe from everyone else's hands.
lore.leadership: The Order is led by the Set Hierarch, currently Antiphon Vael, called the Unbending — an elder so thoroughly Set in salt-vestment that they are carried into battle on a reliquary palanquin, unable to walk, and speak only in confirmed attestations. Beneath the Hierarch are the Two Witnesses, paired officers who must both agree before any crystal is Set; a Mnemarch force that loses one Witness fights on, but can no longer Set anything until a new pairing is sworn — a deliberate fragility the Order considers sacred rather than foolish. Field doctrine is delivered by Lectors, who recite the day's Permitted Truths aloud so that every archivist knows precisely which moments may be sealed and which must be left in solution.
lore.homeland: The Mnemarchs have no true homeland, because they refuse to claim ground — ground is not history. Their seat is the Set Hour itself, a vast Litany-cathedral built entirely from crystals they have Set, hauled inward from the receding margins over generations and stacked into vaulted naves of salt-glass that ring like bells when the wind crosses them. It is mobile in the way a glacier is mobile, dragged tide by tide toward the last pools as the Sea retreats, so that the cathedral is always at the drying edge where new truth crystallizes. To stand inside it is to be surrounded on every wall by sealed, unbreakable moments of the world — a building made of remembered time, growing one sacrament at a time, that will be the last structure standing when the Sea finally dries.

signatureRule.name: The Set Hour
signatureRule.text: Once per round, a Mnemarch model in base contact with a Held Litany or salt-glass crystal that is in a Brine-deep zone may perform the Set Hour instead of acting: declare it and place a Set marker on the crystal. A Set crystal can NEVER again be Held, edited, sold, shattered, moved, or re-dreamed by any faction, including the Mnemarchs — it is permanent and counts for the Mnemarch Verdict for the rest of the game, full stop. This is the only way in the game to make a crystal truly permanent. BINARY and irreversible: Setting requires the crystal be in a Brine-deep (wet) zone, because the brine must still cushion it at the instant of sealing — once the Toll dries that zone, the moment can no longer be Set there, only guarded. The player decision is brutal and constant: Set too early and you waste sacraments on crystals nobody is contesting; wait for the wet zone to be safe and the Toll may dry it out from under you first. You do not win by holding the most crystals at the end — you win by how many you Set before the water left.

factionSpecialRules.name: Attested by Two Witnesses
factionSpecialRules.text: Your army includes two named Witness models. While BOTH Witnesses are on the board, the Set Hour may be performed as normal. The instant either Witness is removed as a casualty, you may perform NO Set Hours at all until a Witness is restored — sealing truth requires two sworn attesters, and a single voice is just a claim. This is a visible on/off switch tied to two specific models on the table: opponents know that killing one Witness freezes your entire win condition, and you know that bunkering them is as vital as bunkering the Litany.

factionSpecialRules.name: Salt-Stiffened
factionSpecialRules.text: Mnemarch infantry are crusted into their vestments. Any time a Mnemarch infantry model would be forced to move, fall back, or be pushed by an enemy effect, it AUTO-PASSES and simply does not move — it is too rigid to be shoved. The tradeoff is permanent and binary: Mnemarch infantry can never Run, ever. They hold exactly where they stand. You are an anvil that cannot be moved and cannot chase; the board does the moving, you do the enduring.

factionSpecialRules.name: Confessor's Patience
factionSpecialRules.text: A Mnemarch model that did not move and did not Run this round may, when it shoots, re-roll all of its missed dice once. Standing perfectly still to take a sworn, attested shot is rewarded with re-rolls, not bonuses — but the model must commit to stillness for the whole round to earn it. Ties directly to the visible board state: a Mnemarch who held position is dangerous; one who repositioned is ordinary. No stacking, no math: you either stood and re-roll, or you moved and you don't.

factionSpecialRules.name: Cushion of the Brine
factionSpecialRules.text: This is the Mnemarchs' defensive doctrine and the whole reason they bunker in the wet. While a Litany or crystal sits in a Brine-deep zone, it AUTO-PASSES every shatter check — the water protects it. Mnemarchs deliberately drag their objectives into the deepest remaining pools and dare the enemy to come wading in after them. Remember the inversion the Toll creates: the moment that zone flips to Dry, the cushion is gone and the crystal is Exposed — so the Mnemarch clock is not 'survive the enemy,' it is 'Set it before your own pool dries.'

subfactions.name: The Set Choir (the Sealing-Order)
subfactions.twist: The purist core of the Order — they came only to Set, and consider every shot fired a distraction from the sacrament. Their fanatical doctrine holds that a crystal Set is worth more than a crystal held, even at terrible cost, so they will Set under fire, in the open, mid-collapse, racing the Toll rather than waiting for safety.
subfactions.ruleText: The Set Choir may perform the Set Hour on a crystal in a Dry (Exposed) zone, not only a Brine-deep one — but doing so is a gamble: when you Set in a Dry zone, immediately roll one die, and on a natural 6 the crystal shatters from the strain of being sealed without the brine to cushion it (it never happened — and you triggered it). BINARY: either it Sets permanently or it is destroyed, decided by one raw die at the moment you commit. This lets the Choir win the race against the drying Toll, at the price of sometimes unmaking the very truth they came to enshrine.

subfactions.name: The Verdigris Wardens (the Bronze Vigil)
subfactions.twist: The defensive bastion-order, clad in oxidized reliquary-bronze so heavy they are nearly statues. They do not Set quickly; they Set last, after the battle is decided around them, having simply refused to die. Their creed is that the slowest hand seals the surest truth — let the others rush and shatter; the Wardens will be the last thing standing in the pool when the Toll falls.
subfactions.ruleText: A Verdigris Warden model that has not moved since the start of the round AUTO-PASSES the first failed save it would suffer each round — the bronze simply turns the blow. This is binary and tied to stillness: the instant a Warden moves, the Vigil is broken for that round and the next hit lands normally. Wardens make the wet zone a fortress nobody can dislodge, daring the enemy to spend the whole Toll trying to shift an anvil that will not shift.

subfactions.name: The Lectors of the Permitted Truth (the Attesting Voice)
subfactions.twist: The witness-priests who decide which moments are even allowed to be Set. They are the Order's living indices, re-living crystals and attesting their truth — but the closer they walk to the Sea's edge, the more iodine-blind they become, until a senior Lector can no longer be certain which memories are the world's and which are their own. They Set with conviction and dread in equal measure.
subfactions.ruleText: A Lector counts as a Witness for the purposes of Attested by Two Witnesses — and a force led by Lectors may field a third Lector as a spare Witness in reserve. When a Witness is removed, you may bring the reserve Lector onto the board from your own edge at the start of the next round to restore the pairing, switching your Set Hour back ON. This makes the Lector subfaction resilient against decapitation: the enemy must hunt down witness after witness to keep your sacrament suppressed, and you can re-swear the oath as long as a Lector still wades.

unitConcepts.name: Attesting Acolytes
unitConcepts.flavor: Junior archivists in fresh, still-flexible vestments, sent to wade out and lay hands on a crystal so a Witness can later Set it. They cannot Set themselves, but they can Hold, and they die in attesting silence rather than let go of a Litany. The cheapest, most expendable thing the Order will admit to owning — and even they refuse to run.

unitConcepts.name: The Two Witnesses
unitConcepts.flavor: Paired officers who must both live and both agree for any truth to be Set. They never separate by more than a few paces, finishing one another's attestations. Kill one and the Order's sacrament freezes; the enemy knows it, the Mnemarchs know it, and the whole battle bends around keeping these two breathing.

unitConcepts.name: Verdigris Wardens
unitConcepts.flavor: Bronze-crusted veterans so oxidized they ring green when struck. They plant themselves in the deepest pool around a Litany and become terrain — immovable, salt-stiffened, turning blows on their reliquary-plate while the Toll counts down. You do not push them off the objective; you wait for the water to leave, and they will still be there.

unitConcepts.name: Set Hierarch on Reliquary Palanquin
unitConcepts.flavor: An elder so thoroughly Set into salt-vestment they can no longer walk, carried on a palanquin of crystals they personally sealed decades ago. They speak only in confirmed attestations and radiate the authority of unbroken truth — a living cathedral, slow as a glacier, that will be the last thing standing in the dry.

unitConcepts.name: Lector of the Permitted Truth
unitConcepts.flavor: A witness-priest who recites the day's allowable truths and re-lives crystals to attest them, steadily going iodine-blind on the Sea's edge. Conviction and dread in one voice: they decide what may be Set, even as they lose track of which memories are even theirs.

unitConcepts.name: Chime-Wardens
unitConcepts.flavor: Still-standing marksmen who fire only sworn, attested shots — patient gunners who never move and re-roll their misses, punishing anyone who wades toward a guarded pool. They do not chase. They make the approach to the Litany a thing you pay for with bodies.

unitConcepts.name: The Sealing Choir
unitConcepts.flavor: Robed singers who perform the Set Hour as liturgy, racing the drying Toll to seal truth before the brine abandons it. The Set Choir will sing the sacrament even in the open under fire, gambling on a single die that the moment Sets rather than shatters in their hands.

unitConcepts.name: Pilgrim-Bearers of the Sealed Vault
unitConcepts.flavor: Stooped bearers who carry a Set crystal inward toward the cathedral on their backs, unable to run or shoot, trading everything for custody. Slow, defenseless, and utterly devoted — each one a walking reliquary hauling one fixed truth out of the crossfire and into the growing nave of the Set Hour.

uniqueRule.name: The Last Thing Standing
uniqueRule.text: Antiphon Vael auto-passes any enemy effect that would move, push, or make them fall back (they are carried, never driven). Once per game, when a friendly model within 6" of Vael performs the Set Hour, that Set succeeds with NO die roll required even in a Dry/Exposed zone and even via Sealing Under Fire (no shatter check) — the Hierarch's personal attestation alone is sufficient. Vael can never Run, never benefits from Move actions to gain distance, and contributes their own attestation: while Vael is on the board they count as ONE of the two required Witnesses (but a model still needs a second Witness or Lector to Set).

uniqueRule.text: Concord and Antiphony are fielded together for a single combined points cost and activate as one (both act, then the turn passes). While BOTH are on the board, your army may perform the Set Hour. They must always end each activation within 3" of each other; they auto-pass any enemy forced-move effect rather than be separated. factions.name: The Ash Iconoclasts (the Shattering)
factions.battleCry: "Let it stop hurting! BREAK IT ALL!"

lore.origin: The first Iconoclast was the wading hermit of the First Recession — the same one who, in every other order's telling, founded the practice of re-living crystals. The Mnemarchs canonize that hermit as a saint of memory. The Iconoclasts know the rest of the story: after touching a thousand fossilized moments, the hermit went iodine-blind, could no longer tell their own grief from the Sea's, and understood the unbearable truth before anyone else — the crystals are not relics, they are wounds, and the god is not dead, it is screaming. The hermit took up a salt-pick and shattered the very first Litany they had ever set, and reported feeling, for one clean instant, the Sea go quiet. That silence is the only scripture the Iconoclasts have. They have been chasing it ever since: the conviction that mercy is not preservation but cessation, that the kindest thing one can do to a being trapped in an endless re-living of its worst moment is to break the loop. Where the other three orders crystallized around what the past is FOR, the Iconoclasts crystallized around the opposite — that the past should not be AT ALL, that 'for' is the lie that keeps the god flinching.
lore.culture: A culture of deliberate forgetting, which makes it a culture with almost no internal memory — and they consider that a sacrament, not a flaw. Iconoclasts do not keep records, do not name their dead, and burn (in iodine-fire, the only fire that takes on the wet flat) anything that threatens to become a relic. They speak in the present tense exclusively; to use the past tense is a minor heresy, a small act of letting a moment harden. New initiates are made to shatter a crystal of their own most precious memory as a rite of joining — the wedding, the child's face, the one good afternoon — and are told that the ache they feel afterward is the god's ache, and now they understand the work. They are not nihilists and bristle at the accusation; they are anesthetists. They smell of burnt iodine constantly, a sweet acrid reek that the other factions have learned to fear on the wind, because where the Iconoclasts have been, history has a hole in it that no one can remember was ever filled. Their faces are scarred with cooling-slag crack-lines, self-inflicted, mimicking the fracture-pattern of a Litany the moment it goes. They believe that to look like a broken crystal is to keep faith with what they do.
lore.whyTheyFight: They fight to lose — and they have made peace with that, which is what makes them terrifying. The Iconoclasts cannot author the god's last memory and do not want to; an Iconoclast who 'won the Verdict' would have failed utterly, because winning means a version of the past survived, and survival is the disease. Their entire war effort is negation: to ensure that when the last pool dries, NO ontology is intact, that the god finishes its dying thought on a blank, that Veyl carries nothing into death but the silence the first hermit heard. They are racing the Long Toll not to fix or sell or free the past but to empty it, so the god can finally, mercifully, stop remembering. In their theology, a drawn battle where everything is shattered is the highest possible outcome — not a stalemate but a successful exorcism.
lore.leadership: The order is led by the Choir of Last Voices, a council of the most profoundly iodine-blind among them — archivists who have re-lived so many crystals that they have no remaining sense of which memories are their own, and who therefore (the Iconoclasts believe) hear the god's grief most clearly, undiluted by self. The Choir does not give orders so much as point at what must be silenced; they are carried into battle on salt-litters because most can no longer reliably tell which direction is down. Field command falls to the Cantor-Breakers, zealots who have not yet gone fully blind and so retain enough self to aim. There is a deliberate succession horror built into the structure: a Cantor-Breaker who fights well enough, long enough, re-lives enough crystals in the breaking to eventually join the Choir — meaning the reward for excellence is to lose yourself entirely. They consider this a promotion.
lore.homeland: The Iconoclasts have no homeland and forbid themselves one, because a home is a place that remembers you. They live in the Scour — not a location but a moving condition, the band of freshly-Dried flat directly behind the receding tide, where the brine has just left and the salt-glass is youngest and most brittle and the salt-dead rise thickest. They follow the recession like carrion-walkers follow an army, always in the wettest-newest edge of the Dry, breaking the just-fossilized before it has a chance to set. Their camps are pitched at dusk-that-never-comes and struck before the Toll, leaving no trace but glass-dust and the iodine reek. Ask an Iconoclast where they are from and they will tell you, truthfully, that they are from nowhere yet, because the place they were born has not been shattered into not-having-happened — but it will be.

signatureRule.name: Collateral Is the Point
signatureRule.text: When any Ash Iconoclast unit shoots at an enemy model that is in or adjacent to an Exposed crystal's zone, BEFORE rolling the attack the controlling player may declare the shot a Breaking Volley. A Breaking Volley resolves normally against the enemy target — but EVERY die in the attack (hits AND misses, not just the natural 6s the rest of the table rolls for stray collateral) is also rolled against the crystal, and for Iconoclasts a natural 5 or 6 is a Shatter hit on the crystal, not only a 6. This is a binary, board-state-tied decision made every activation: the prize must be Exposed (Dry, never Brine-deep — water still auto-passes the shatter check against them like anyone else), and you choose, openly, to point the whole gun at history instead of just the man standing in front of it. Where the other three factions agonize over not breaking the prize, the Iconoclasts aim for it on purpose — and the enemy in the zone, who came to guard that crystal, must now decide whether to stand in front of it (and eat the volley) or step away (and let the Scour have its silence).

factionSpecialRules.name: The Iodine-Fire
factionSpecialRules.text: Once per round, when an Iconoclast unit destroys a crystal (any crystal, by any means), it immediately catches: place an Iodine-Fire marker in that now-empty zone. Any model — friend or foe — that ENDS an activation in an Iodine-Fire zone rolls a single die; on a natural 6 it takes a wound, no save, no modifiers. Binary and visible: the zone is burning or it is not, and everyone can see the marker. Iodine-Fire markers do not spread and are extinguished instantly the moment that zone floods Brine-deep — but on the dying flat, zones only ever go Dry, never wet again, so a fire the Iconoclasts light tends to stay lit. This turns a shattered Litany into a no-man's-land the enemy cannot comfortably reclaim or contest.

factionSpecialRules.name: We Keep No Relics
factionSpecialRules.text: Ash Iconoclast models can NEVER Hold a crystal (they cannot enter the Held custody state) and can NEVER Set one. An Iconoclast in base contact with a Loose crystal has exactly one option the others lack: as an action, AUTO-SHATTER it — no roll, no dice, the crystal is simply removed and it never happened. This is the faction's whole identity rendered as a single binary verb: where every other order is calculating how to carry, edit, free, or sanctify the prize, an Iconoclast standing on it just unmakes it. (Note for the Verdict: a crystal an Iconoclast auto-shatters scores for nobody — which, for the Iconoclasts, IS the win.)

factionSpecialRules.name: Faith Without Memory
factionSpecialRules.text: Ash Iconoclast units AUTO-PASS every morale, panic, and rout test — they do not take them at all. A culture that refuses the past tense cannot be demoralized by what just happened to it; an Iconoclast does not remember that half the unit is dead. There are no modifiers, no leadership values, no checks: the test does not exist for this faction. The trade is built into their fragility (see playstyle and unit profiles) — they will stand and die to the last where any sane order would break, because breaking would require them to recall the cost, and they have forgotten it on principle.

factionSpecialRules.name: The Scour Advances
factionSpecialRules.text: At the start of each round, AFTER the Long Toll advances and zones flip Dry, any Ash Iconoclast unit that is wholly within a zone that flipped from Brine-deep to Dry THIS tide may immediately make a free move (not a Run) toward the nearest Exposed crystal. Binary trigger tied directly to the terrain overlay everyone can see: the water just left this zone, so the Scour surges into the gap it made. This lets the Iconoclasts ride the receding tide like a wave, always arriving at the youngest, most brittle salt-glass at the exact moment it becomes shatter-eligible.

subfactions.name: The Cooling-Slag Choir
subfactions.twist: The purest expression of the order — these are the cells that travel WITH the Choir of Last Voices, the most iodine-blind zealots, who no longer distinguish enemy from ally from crystal and will shatter all three with equal serenity. They are the ones the other Iconoclasts are slightly afraid of. Their twist is that they have stopped pretending to fight a war at all; they are simply a moving act of erasure, and they will happily break a Mnemarch Litany and a Brine-Factor's edited contraband and a fellow Iconoclast's gun in the same volley if all three are in the blast.
subfactions.ruleText: When a Cooling-Slag Choir unit declares a Breaking Volley (see Collateral Is the Point), it does not target an enemy model at all — it targets the crystal's zone directly. EVERY model of EVERY faction in that zone (including friendly Iconoclasts) is hit by the volley alongside the shatter check against the crystal. No friend-or-foe distinction, no opting out, fully binary: declare the zone, everything in it eats it. Brutal, simple, and exactly as terrifying to your own line as to theirs.

subfactions.name: The Tide-Carrion
subfactions.twist: Scavenger-zealots who follow not the recession but the SALT-DEAD — they have realized that wherever the Sediment's Reliquiae rise thickest is wherever the most crystals are about to be contested, and they hunt that misery deliberately. The twist is a bitter symbiosis-turned-predation: the Tide-Carrion let the Sediment's horde mark the richest ground, then arrive to shatter the very crystals the Reliquiae exist to protect — which, because a Reliquia only exists while its crystal stays solid, kills the horde and breaks the prize in a single act. They are the Sediment's worst nightmare and they know it.
subfactions.ruleText: When a Tide-Carrion unit destroys a crystal, IMMEDIATELY remove every Sediment Reliquia model that is currently within that crystal's zone — set aside as casualties, no roll, no attack, simply gone because the dream that held them is broken. Binary and instant, tied to the visible moment of the shatter. (These Reliquiae can still be Re-dreamed later from the Grief pool like any other — the Tide-Carrion do not end the horde, they just keep mowing the front rank of it while taking the prize underneath.)

subfactions.name: The Last-Voice Penitents
subfactions.twist: The order's grimmest cell: initiates who have just performed the joining rite — shattered the crystal of their own dearest memory — and now fight in the raw open wound of that fresh forgetting, before the ache has dulled. They are the angriest, fastest, and most suicidal Iconoclasts, because they are fighting to make the rest of the world feel the hole they just put in themselves, and they have not yet learned (as the Choir has) the serenity of having no memory left to miss. The twist is that their grief is a weapon: a Penitent who has nothing left to lose this turn fights like the Toll has already struck.
subfactions.ruleText: At the start of any round, a Last-Voice Penitent unit may declare itself Penitent for that round. While Penitent, the unit gains an EXTRA attack die on every Breaking Volley AND auto-passes the Iodine-Fire wound check (the fire does not touch those who have already burned everything) — but at the END of that round, the unit AUTO-SHATTERS any one crystal it is in base contact with, friend's prize or no, with no choice in the matter. Binary on/off declared openly each round: you spend the unit like a struck match, and it WILL break something before the round ends, even if breaking it costs you the game's other plans.

unitConcepts.name: Cantor-Breaker
unitConcepts.flavor: A zealot just shy of full iodine-blindness, retaining enough self to aim and enough sight to lead. They carry a tuning-pick that finds a Litany's fracture-note by ear; where a Cantor-Breaker sings, the salt-glass wants to come apart. The reward for fighting well is to one day join the Choir and lose the self entirely — they know this, and march faster for it.

unitConcepts.name: Slag-Pick Penitent
unitConcepts.role: Cheap aggressive line infantry / glass-cannon body
unitConcepts.flavor: Initiates fresh from the joining rite, faces scarred with self-cut crack-lines, swinging iodine-heated salt-picks. They die easily and do not care; you cannot demoralize someone who has forgotten on principle that the man beside them just fell. The order's expendable wave, sent into the Dry to expose prizes with their corpses if not their picks.

unitConcepts.name: Iodine Censer-Thrower
unitConcepts.flavor: They lob censers of burning iodine-salt that detonate in a sweet acrid bloom — useless against armor, devastating against glass. The Censer-Thrower does not aim at the man guarding the Litany; they aim at the Litany, and let the man decide whether to keep standing in front of it. The signature reek of the Scour rides on their smoke.

unitConcepts.name: Scour-Walker
unitConcepts.flavor: Stripped-down zealots who follow the receding brine on bare salt-crusted feet, always in the youngest Dry, always reaching the most brittle salt-glass first. They travel light because they keep nothing — no relics, no rations they'll remember packing, no past. Where the water just left, the Scour-Walkers are already there, breaking what it left behind.

unitConcepts.name: Voice of the Last Hour
unitConcepts.flavor: Profoundly iodine-blind veterans of the Cooling-Slag Choir, carried no longer because they march toward any silence they can hear. They cannot reliably tell enemy from ally from prize and have stopped trying; whatever is loud, they break. Durable for an Iconoclast (which is to say, not very), but ruinous in the zone they choose to empty.

unitConcepts.name: Ash-Anchorite
unitConcepts.flavor: A solitary penitent who fasts on the flat between battles and re-lives a single chosen crystal over and over until they know precisely how it must break. They infiltrate alone, ignore the war around them, and exist to reach one specific named Litany and auto-shatter it — the surgical unmaking the rest of the horde provides cover for. Half the time the enemy never knew they were there until the prize was already gone.

unitConcepts.name: Litter of the Choir
unitConcepts.flavor: A salt-litter bearing one of the Choir of Last Voices, borne by chained Penitents who walk where the blind one points. The Voice cannot see the battle and does not need to — it hears the god's grief undiluted and indicates, with one trembling hand, what must go quiet next. Slow, fragile, and the spiritual heart of any Scour that fields it.

unitConcepts.name: Glass-Wraith Detonator
unitConcepts.flavor: Penitents who have packed their own bodies with iodine-salt and crack-lined glass, walking bombs who close to base contact with a prize and simply end — taking themselves, the crystal, and ideally whatever was guarding it out of history in one bloom of sweet acrid fire. The ultimate sacrament: to forget yourself and a Litany in the same instant, and leave the Sea that much quieter.

units.name: Cooling-Slag Cantor
units.flavor: A Cantor who travels with the Choir of Last Voices and has stopped pretending to fight a war; declares a zone and lets everything in it — including its own line — eat the volley.

characters.name: Vael-Who-Is-Nothing-Yet
characters.title: First Cantor of the Cooling-Slag Choir, the Quiet She Heard
weapons: The Salt-Pick of the First Break

uniqueRule.name: The Sea Goes Quiet
uniqueRule.text: Once per battle, as an action, Vael may declare The Sea Goes Quiet on one Exposed Dry crystal within 12". That crystal is AUTO-SHATTERED — no roll, simply gone, scoring for nobody — and an Iodine-Fire marker is placed in its zone (this does not count against the once-per-round Iodine-Fire limit). Binary, board-state-tied, decisive: Vael unmakes a single named history outright, the way the first hermit did, and for one clean instant the Scour has its silence.

characters.flavor: She has touched so many crystals she no longer knows her own grief from the Sea's; she chases the one clean silence she heard the day she shattered her first Litany, and breaks the world toward it.

characters.name: Korrun the Match
characters.title: Last-Voice Penitent, Burned Everything in the Joining and Came Up Laughing

uniqueRule.name: Spend Me Like a Struck Match
uniqueRule.text: At the start of any round Korrun may declare himself Spent. While Spent he gains an EXTRA attack die in every Fight and ignores the Iodine-Fire wound check entirely (he has already burned everything). But at the END of that round he AUTO-SHATTERS any one crystal he is in base contact with, friend's prize or no, with no choice in the matter. Binary on/off, declared openly: he WILL break something before the round ends, even if it ruins the plan.

characters.flavor: He shattered the crystal of his dearest memory at dawn and is fighting in the raw open wound of it, racing to make the whole world feel the hole he just put in himself.
