scenarios.name: The Reckoning of the Sixth Toll
scenarios.hook: Veyl is dying with the tide. For six hundred years the Litany Sea has covered the Choir-Floor of Saint Marrow's Reach, and for six hundred years the crystals set into that floor have stayed solid, wet, and unreadable — a library nobody could open because nobody could reach it. Now the brine is leaving for the last time. The Long Toll has begun: one notch of the sea drains each time the bell-buoys ring, and every faction on the shore can hear exactly how much water is left. When the Sixth Toll strikes Dry, the Choir-Floor is bare forever and the Sea will never return to cushion the glass again. The Mnemarchs have come to Set the floor's memory into eternity before it can be read. The Iconoclasts have come to put a gun to that same history and silence it the instant the water uncovers it. The Brine-Factors have come to pry the crystals loose and sell the past by weight before either zealot can decide its fate. And under all of them, in every receding inch, Veyl's grief is already re-dreaming the drowned. Nobody controls the clock. Everyone obeys it. The only question is what is left standing — and intact — when the water finishes leaving the table.
scenarios.setup: Play on a board divided into SIX numbered tidal bands running parallel to the shore edge, Band 1 (nearest shore) to Band 6 (deepest sea). Each band is covered by a double-sided terrain overlay: WET side up = Brine-deep, DRY side up = exposed Choir-Floor. At game start, ALL six bands are WET (Brine-deep). Place the Tide Track beside the board, a fixed strip of six notches labelled Toll I through Toll VI, with the Tide marker resting before Toll I. Place ONE Litany crystal model in the centre of each band — six crystals total, all starting Loose and all starting in Brine-deep zones (so all six begin shatter-immune). Crystals 1-2 are minor (1 Shatter destroys), crystals 3-4 are major (2 Shatters), crystals 5-6 are the Choir-Cantors (3 Shatters, worth double at Verdict). Set the Grief pool beside the Tide Track, starting empty. The Sediment player sets aside their full Reliquiae horde off-board in the Salt-dead reserve — none deploy at the start.
scenarios.deployment: Four-player free-for-all. The three living factions (Mnemarchs, Ash Iconoclasts, Brine-Factors) deploy along the SHORE edge only, within 6" of the board edge behind Band 1 — i.e. on dry land, with the entire wet sea between them and the deepest crystals. Roll off for deployment order; place alternately. No living model may begin in a Brine-deep band (you start on the shore and must advance into the receding tide as it opens). The Sediment (Veyl's swarm) does not deploy a starting force; the Sediment player instead takes the Grief pool and the Salt-dead reserve, and re-dreams Reliquiae onto the board as the Long Toll opens Dry ground for them (see Special Rules). The shore edge belongs to no faction — it is the only fixed land, and the Verdict is scored from whoever holds intact crystals when the Sixth Toll falls, not from territory.
scenarios.objectives: Primary: control the most VALUE in INTACT crystals when the Sixth Toll strikes Dry and the game ends. A crystal scores for the player whose model is in base contact (Held), who has Set it (Mnemarch), or who has Liquidated it to the Hold (Brine-Factor) — a Loose crystal nobody controls scores for nobody, and a Shattered crystal scores for nobody and never did. Each living faction races the silent Toll Deck to LOCK value in before a rival contests it: Mnemarchs Set crystals in WET bands (sealed forever); Brine-Factors carry Loose crystals to the shore and Liquidate them into Coin (off-board, unsealable, un-re-dreamable); Iconoclasts deny all value by Shattering Exposed crystals in DRY bands so no one scores them. The Sediment does not score crystals — it wins by feeding the Grief engine, Drowning sales, and erasing enough meaning that the drowned belong to the tide and not to any owner. The board, the Tide Track, and the Grief pool are the entire score sheet.
scenarios.victory: At the instant the Sixth Toll strikes (end of Round 6), the game ends immediately mid-action — no further activations. Tally VALUE: minor crystals 1, major crystals 2, Choir-Cantors 4. A crystal counts ONLY if it is intact AND in a scoring state for that player: Set crystals score for the Mnemarch who sealed them; Coin (Liquidated) crystals score for the Brine-Factor who sold them; Loose-but-Held crystals score for the model in base contact. Shattered crystals are worth nothing to everyone. The Sediment player does NOT score crystals — the Sediment WINS by ATTRITION OF MEANING: if the total VALUE of Shattered + Drowned-and-uncontrolled crystals (crystals left Loose in a Reliquia-occupied band at game end) EQUALS OR EXCEEDS the highest single living faction's banked value, Veyl wins — the past returned to the tide instead of to any owner. Otherwise, the living faction with the highest banked VALUE wins. Tiebreak among living factions: most Set/Coin crystals (permanence beats mere possession), then most Choir-Cantors held.
scenarios.length: 6 rounds — one per Toll. The Tide Track IS the round counter and it is mandatory and unskippable.
scenarios.twist: The tide does not drain in band order — it drains in a SECRET PROGRAMMED SEQUENCE revealed one notch at a time. Before the game, shuffle six band-tiles (numbered 1-6) face down into a Toll Deck. At the START of each round, before any activation, flip the top Toll Deck tile: THAT band flips from Wet to Dry this round (advance the Tide marker one notch as the bell rings). Players know SIX bands will dry over six rounds and they can hear the Toll coming, but they never know WHICH band the sea abandons next until the tile turns — so the shore-line does not recede in a tidy wall. A band that dries early exposes its crystal to shatter and to Iconoclast volleys for many rounds; a band that stays wet until Toll V protects its crystal but leaves almost no time to Set, Hold, or Liquidate it before the end. Everyone commits to advancing into the sea blind to which ground will betray them, and the deepest Choir-Cantors (Bands 5-6, the highest value) may not surface until it is nearly too late to claim them intact. The clock is loud; the order is silent.

specialRules.name: The Long Toll (mandatory clock)
specialRules.text: At the START of every round, ring the Toll: flip the top tile of the Toll Deck and turn that band's overlay from WET (Brine-deep) to DRY (exposed Choir-Floor), then advance the Tide marker one notch. This is automatic, unskippable, and identical for all players — no faction, model, or rule may delay, hasten, skip, or reorder a Toll. The instant a band goes Dry: its crystal becomes Exposed (shatter-eligible), it loses Brine cushioning forever, and the Grief pool gains 1 token. When the Sixth Toll strikes, the game ends immediately. Time is the water leaving the table; you read the round off the board, never off a count in your head.

specialRules.name: Brine Cushion (auto-pass while wet)
specialRules.text: A crystal in a WET (Brine-deep) band AUTO-PASSES every shatter check — the water cushions the glass, period. No roll, no modifier: wet is safe, full stop. The instant its band flips Dry on the Toll, that protection is gone and stays gone — the sea never re-covers a band. This is a pure BINARY on/off tied to the visible overlay: look at the tile, you know if the crystal can break.

specialRules.name: Collateral Shatter (Sixes, raw)
specialRules.text: When any attack's shots MISS a target that is in or adjacent to a Dry band containing an Exposed crystal, the attacker immediately rolls those missed dice against the crystal. Each natural 6 is a Shatter hit — no modifiers, no re-rolls from other sources, just raw Sixes. Accumulate Shatters equal to the crystal's toughness (minor 1 / major 2 / Cantor 3) and it is destroyed and removed: it never happened, nobody scores it, and the Grief pool gains 1. Every shot taken near the prize is a BINARY gamble — take the risky volley, or hold fire.

specialRules.name: Custody & the Ignore-X of Carrying
specialRules.text: A crystal is Loose, Held (a model in base contact controls it), or Set (permanent). A model may pick up a Loose crystal in its band and carry it: a CARRYING model may NOT Run and may NOT shoot — it trades all mobility and firepower for custody (IGNORE-X: it ignores its own ranged actions entirely while it holds the Litany). Drop the crystal and the model is normal again next activation. This is the central tradeoff: every model carrying history is a model not fighting.

specialRules.name: The Set Hour (wet-only seal)
specialRules.text: A Mnemarch model in base contact with a crystal in a WET band may perform the Set Hour: the crystal becomes Set — permanently sealed, immune to all further capture, shatter, sale, and re-dreaming, scoring for that Mnemarch at the Verdict. Set can ONLY happen while the band is still wet. The moment the Toll dries that band, the window is closed forever. Mnemarchs must reach the deep crystals BEFORE the sea abandons them — racing the silent Toll Deck to seal what the Iconoclasts are waiting to silence.

specialRules.name: The Breaking Volley (dry-only silence)
specialRules.text: An Ash Iconoclast model may declare a Breaking Volley at an Exposed crystal in a DRY band: it shoots the crystal directly, each natural 6 a Shatter (raw Sixes, no modifiers). The Volley can ONLY target Dry bands — over wet water every Iconoclast shot auto-fails the Brine Cushion. Iconoclast and Mnemarch are mirror enemies across the tideline: the Set Hour only works wet, the Breaking Volley only works dry, so whoever owns the exact moment a band flips owns whether that crystal is sealed forever or silenced forever.

specialRules.name: Re-dreaming the Drowned (Grief engine)
specialRules.text: At the start of each round, AFTER the Toll, the Sediment player may spend Grief tokens to Re-dream set-aside Reliquiae back onto the board into any DRY band (auto-return, no roll — 1 token per Reliquia). A Reliquia removed as a casualty is set aside, not destroyed, and can be re-dreamed again. The swarm grows precisely as the table degrades: every Shatter and every Toll feeds Grief, so the more violence the three living factions do, the larger Veyl's horde re-dreams. The Grief pool is the only bookkeeping and it sits face-up beside the clock.

specialRules.name: Tide-Erasure (gone when dry, twice over)
specialRules.text: A Reliquia standing in a WET band that recedes to Dry on the Toll is NOT erased — it survives the first time the tide passes over it, and it IGNORES the casualty rules while it stood wet. But any Reliquia the tide passes over a SECOND time (still on the board in a band when a later Toll would re-expose it, i.e. caught in a band that dries while it stands there a second tidal step) IS erased — removed permanently, not set aside, no re-dream. The swarm is on while wet, gone when twice-dry: a visible on/off tied entirely to the terrain overlay, no token to track.

specialRules.name: Drown the Sale (deny the Hold)
specialRules.text: A Reliquia in base contact with a Loose crystal at the moment its band goes Dry Drowns it: the crystal stays Loose and contested and may NOT be Liquidated, Set, or carried off that round while a Reliquia holds base contact. This is the Sediment's answer to the Brine-Factors — the Factor wants the crystal off the table into untouchable Coin, the Sediment keeps it in the receding water and in play. A BINARY lock: Reliquia in contact = no sale, no seal, this activation.

scenarios.name: The Reliquary Run
scenarios.hook: When the Sea first began to leave, the Mnemarchs hid their holiest Litany — the Choir-Crystal called Nine Mouths, which remembers the exact sound Veyl made when it learned its dead were dead — in the deepest brine-pit on the shelf, trusting the water to guard it. Now the water is leaving. As the tide recedes pit by pit, Nine Mouths and a scatter of lesser Litanies are surfacing into the open air for the first time in an age, naked and shatter-eligible under four sets of guns. The Mnemarchs come to carry them home and Set them forever. The Brine-Factors come to haul them off the shelf and into the Hold before they can be sealed. The Ash Iconoclasts come to do what they always do to surfacing history: point and break. And the Sediment do not come at all — they are already here, dreamed back into every drying pit, reaching up out of the salt for anything warm enough to drag under. Whoever carries history off this shelf intact owns it. Whoever fumbles it gives it to the dark.
scenarios.setup: Play on a roughly 4x4 board divided into a 4x4 grid of sixteen zones. Build the board entirely from double-sided terrain overlays (wet side up / dry side up) so every zone can flip on the Toll. At game start, the OUTER ring of twelve zones is Brine-deep (wet side up); the inner 2x2 of four zones — the Choir-Pit — is also Brine-deep. Place crystal models as physical objects: ONE Choir-Crystal (Nine Mouths, a large model, the Prize) Loose at the dead center of the Choir-Pit, and FIVE lesser Litany crystals Loose, one in each of five randomly chosen outer zones. All six crystals begin in Brine-deep zones, so all six begin protected (AUTO-PASS shatter). Set up the Tide Track at 6 tides. Place the Grief pool marker at zero. The Tide flips zones inward: tide 1 flips the four CORNER zones to Dry, tides 2-5 flip the remaining outer ring in toward the center, and tide 6 flips the inner Choir-Pit to Dry — the Prize surfaces last and the Toll strikes Dry the instant it does.
scenarios.deployment: Four factions, four board edges, deployed in that turn order: Mnemarchs, Brine-Factors, Ash Iconoclasts, Sediment. The first three deploy along their own board edge, no model within one zone of any crystal. The Sediment do NOT deploy a force — instead the Sediment player places NOTHING at start and is given the Grief pool: they bring models onto the board only by Re-dreaming Reliquiae out of drying pits (see special rules). The Choir-Crystal at center is equidistant from all three edge factions by design — nobody can reach it before the tide does.
scenarios.objectives: The prize is custody of intact history, not a body count. Crystals score ONLY for the faction that controls them in their winning custody state when the Toll strikes Dry. A shattered crystal scores for NO ONE — it never happened. Each faction scores its OWN custody state: Mnemarchs score Set crystals; Brine-Factors score crystals taken OFF the board into the Hold; Iconoclasts score crystals they personally Shattered; Sediment score crystals that are Loose in a Dry zone they occupy (Drowned). The Choir-Crystal (Nine Mouths) is worth triple any lesser Litany to whoever's victory state it ends in.
scenarios.victory: At the Toll Dry (end of round 6), tally Custody Points. Lesser Litany = 1 point in your winning state; Nine Mouths = 3 points. Mnemarchs: +1 per Set crystal. Brine-Factors: +1 per crystal carried off any board edge into the Hold. Iconoclasts: +1 per crystal they Shattered this game (the ONLY faction that scores destruction — silence is their victory). Sediment: +1 per Loose crystal in a Dry zone containing a Sediment model and no enemy model. Most Custody Points wins. TIEBREAK, in order: (1) controls Nine Mouths' final state, (2) fewest friendly crystals shattered by accident, (3) most enemy models still on the shelf when the water left.
scenarios.length: 6 rounds (one full Tide Track; the Toll strikes Dry at the end of round 6)
scenarios.twist: THE PIT REMEMBERS WHAT IT DROWNED. The Choir-Crystal, Nine Mouths, sits in the last pit to dry — and it is not empty. When tide 6 flips the Choir-Pit to Dry and the Prize finally surfaces Exposed, the Grief pool DISCHARGES: the Sediment player immediately Re-dreams up to their full Grief total of Reliquiae into the four Choir-Pit zones at once, AUTO-RETURN, surrounding whoever was reaching for the Prize. The faction that rushed center early to be first on Nine Mouths is now alone in a flooding pit of the dead — but anyone who hung back let the tide and three rivals get there first. The whole game the other players have been feeding that pool every time they shattered a crystal or let a zone dry; the Iconoclasts especially have been arming the very ambush that decides the Prize.

specialRules.name: Custody States (the binary that replaces 'control')
specialRules.text: Every crystal is a physical model in exactly one of three states, readable at a glance. LOOSE: on the board, claimed by nobody. HELD: a model is in base contact — that model controls it but pays the Carry Tax. SET: permanently locked (Mnemarch-only). To claim a Loose crystal, end an activation in base contact: it becomes Held. Custody is BINARY — a crystal is Held or it is not; there is no contested-control arithmetic. If the carrier dies or breaks contact, the crystal drops Loose where it stands.

specialRules.name: The Carry Tax (IGNORE-X, not a penalty stack)
specialRules.text: A model carrying a Held crystal CANNOT Run and CANNOT shoot — it ignores those actions entirely while it carries (IGNORE Run, IGNORE Shoot). It may still walk and may still fight in melee. This is the core trade of the scenario: a carrier is a courier, not a soldier. Hand-off is legal — touch a friendly model in base contact and pass the crystal as a free action — so factions form bucket-brigades down the drying tideline rather than one hero sprinting the whole board.

specialRules.name: Collateral on the Miss (Custody & Collateral)
specialRules.text: Whenever an attack is made into or adjacent to an Exposed crystal's zone, every MISSED shot is re-rolled once against the crystal itself: each natural 6 is a Shatter hit (raw dice, no modifiers — pure Sixes). Three accumulated Shatters destroys a crystal: remove it, nobody scores it, and add a Grief token. This is the constant decision every activation: the clean shot at an enemy near the Prize might erase the Prize. Hold fire and stay safe, or fire and gamble history.

specialRules.name: Wet Cushions Glass (AUTO-PASS, tied to the overlay)
specialRules.text: A crystal in a Brine-deep (wet-side-up) zone AUTO-PASSES every shatter check — the water cushions the glass, so you may blaze away near it freely. The instant the Toll flips that zone to Dry (dry-side-up), the crystal is Exposed and Collateral on the Miss is live. The terrain overlay alone tells every player what is safe to shoot near this round; protection moves inward and vanishes pit by pit as the Sea leaves.

specialRules.name: The Set Hour (Mnemarchs) vs. The Breaking Volley (Iconoclasts)
specialRules.text: MNEMARCHS may attempt to SET a Held crystal ONLY while its zone is still Brine-deep (wet) — roll the Sealing Choir; on any natural 6 it is Set forever and can never be Shattered, Held, Drowned, or carried to the Hold by anyone. ICONOCLASTS' Breaking Volley may target a crystal directly ONLY in a Dry zone (where it is Exposed): every natural 6 is a Shatter, no miss step needed. The tideline is the tug-of-war — own the wet side and you can seal; own the dry side and you can break. Whoever controls the moment a zone flips owns that crystal's fate.

specialRules.name: Re-dream the Drowned (Sediment / The Dreaming Grief)
specialRules.text: The Grief pool gains a token whenever ANY crystal Shatters or ANY zone flips to Dry (all factions trigger it). At the start of each round the Sediment spend Grief to Re-dream set-aside Reliquiae onto the board in any Dry zone, AUTO-RETURN, no roll. A Reliquia is removed as a casualty is only set ASIDE, not destroyed, and can be re-dreamed again — UNLESS the tide passes over its zone a second time while it stands there, which erases it for good (IGNORE death while wet-then-dry once; gone on the second drying). The horde grows exactly as the board degrades.

scenarios.concept: Custody & Collateral: capture the fragile prize without shattering it.

scenarios.name: The Sealing of the Last Shoal
scenarios.hook: Veyl's grief dreams loudest at the Last Shoal, a reef of seven Litany-crystals that holds the only un-erased memory of the god's first death. The Sealing Choir of the Mnemarchs has waded out at low brine to perform the Set Hour and lock the Shoal beyond all commerce and all silence — forever. But the Long Toll has already begun, and the Ash Iconoclasts have read the same falling water. Each notch the Sea takes, another band of the Shoal goes Dry, and dry glass can be broken. The Choir does not need to win. It needs to last. The Iconoclasts do not need to take ground. They need to be standing on the right band of mud at the exact moment the water abandons it — and to pull the trigger before the Sealing prayer finishes. Whoever owns the tideline owns whether the first death of a god is remembered forever, or shouted into nothing.
scenarios.setup: Play on a 4x4 board divided into six numbered tide bands (1 nearest the dry shore, 6 furthest out to sea). Every band starts Brine-deep (wet side up) EXCEPT band 1, which begins Dry. Place SEVEN Litany-crystal models in a rough arc across the Shoal: one each in bands 1 and 6, two in band 2, and three clustered in bands 3 and 4 (the heart of the reef). All seven crystals begin Loose and Un-set. Build a physical Tide Track of six notches; place the Tide marker on notch 1. Place an empty Grief pool dish beside the board. Each band is a double-sided terrain overlay: wet side up = Brine-deep (auto-pass shatter, no Set possible), dry side up = Dry (Exposed crystals, Sealing possible). Set aside a reserve of Reliquiae models off-board next to the Grief pool — these belong to neither player and are controlled by the attacker (see twist).
scenarios.deployment: ASYMMETRIC. The MNEMARCHS (defender) deploy first, anywhere in bands 4, 5, and 6 (the still-wet heart and seaward edge of the Shoal), in base contact with or within 3 inches of the crystals they intend to seal. The defender may declare any number of models as Choristers at deployment. The ASH ICONOCLASTS (attacker) deploy second, entirely along the dry shore edge behind band 1 — they begin on land, the wrong side of the water, and must advance INTO the receding sea as it dries before them. No attacker model may deploy past the band-1/band-2 line. The attacker has the first activation of round 1.
scenarios.objectives: The crystals are the only objective; ground is worthless. A crystal scores for the side that owns its final state when the Toll strikes Dry. A crystal is SEALED (scores for the Mnemarchs) if a Chorister completed the Set Hour on it. A crystal is SILENCED (scores for the Iconoclasts) if it was Shattered and removed. A crystal that ends the game Loose, Un-set, and intact scores for NEITHER side. Count Sealed crystals for the defender and Silenced crystals for the attacker at the final Toll.
scenarios.victory: At the end of round 6, when the Toll strikes Dry, compare totals. The MNEMARCHS win if they have Sealed FOUR or more of the seven crystals. The ASH ICONOCLASTS win if they have Silenced FOUR or more. If neither side reaches four — because too many crystals ended Loose and intact, or because the Reliquiae horde Drowned the contested zones — the result is the Grey Verdict: the Long Toll wins, the Shoal is neither remembered nor silenced, and the player holding the FEWER Grief tokens' worth of board corruption (i.e. who caused less erasure) takes a marginal moral victory. Sealing and Silencing the SAME crystal is impossible by definition; each crystal can only ever be in one final state.
scenarios.twist: THE SHOAL DROWNS ITSELF. The Iconoclasts cannot simply rush band 1, because Shattering feeds the Grief pool — and the Grief horde belongs to the attacker to place but answers to no one's victory. Every crystal Shattered and every band that flips Dry drops a token in the Grief pool. At the start of each round, BEFORE the Toll advances, the ATTACKER must spend all available Grief tokens to Re-dream set-aside Reliquiae into any Dry bands (auto-return, no roll, one Reliquia per token). The attacker controls these models in movement and shooting — but a Reliquia standing on a crystal makes that crystal Loose-locked: it cannot be Sealed (it blocks the Chorister) AND it cannot be cleanly Silenced for score (a Reliquia-occupied crystal that shatters scores for nobody, it just feeds more Grief). So the Iconoclast's own violence summons a swarm that converts contested crystals into worthless Grey outcomes. Break too much, too fast, and you drown your own victory: the seventh round never comes, but the Shoal you wanted to silence is instead simply gone, claimed by Veyl's dreaming, scoring for no one. The attacker must Silence with surgical restraint, not a Breaking storm.
scenarios.length: 6 rounds (the Tide Track is fixed at six notches; the game ends immediately when the Toll strikes Dry at the end of round 6).

specialRules.name: The Long Toll Advances (the wandering tideline)
specialRules.text: At the start of every round, AFTER the attacker re-dreams Grief, advance the Tide marker one notch. The newly-indexed band flips from Brine-deep to Dry: turn that band's overlay wet-side-down to dry-side-up. This is mandatory, unskippable, identical for both players, and instant. Order of bands going dry is FIXED and known to all from turn one: band 1 is already Dry; then band 2 (start of round 2), band 3 (round 3), and so on out to band 6 at the start of round 6. No faction speeds or slows it. Each flip drops one token in the Grief pool. Every player can see exactly how many rounds of protection any crystal has left simply by reading where the water is — no turn-counting in your head, the water tells you. Decision created: the defender must Seal seaward crystals LAST (they stay wet longest) and shoreward crystals are already lost; the attacker must position the round BEFORE a band dries so the Breaking Volley can land the instant it flips.

specialRules.name: The Set Hour (Mnemarch sealing ritual)
specialRules.text: A Chorister in base contact with a Loose crystal that is in a BRINE-DEEP (wet) band may, as its full activation, perform the Set Hour: roll one die — a natural 6 (Sixes: raw dice, no modifiers) Sets the crystal permanently (Sealed, scores for the Mnemarchs, can never be Shattered, sold, or Held). On any other result the ritual continues — place a Choir marker; on this Chorister's NEXT activation, if still in base contact and the band is still wet, the crystal auto-Sets (no second roll needed). BINARY board-state gate: the Set Hour can ONLY be attempted or completed in a wet band. The instant the Toll dries that band, any in-progress Choir marker is washed away and the ritual fails. This is the whole defender clock: seal it while the water still cushions it, or lose the chance forever when the band goes Dry.

specialRules.name: The Breaking Volley (Iconoclast shatter-fire)
specialRules.text: An Iconoclast model that did not Run this activation may declare a Breaking Volley at a crystal in a DRY band within range and line of sight. Roll the model's shooting dice with NO modifiers; each natural 6 is a Shatter hit. A crystal needs 2 Shatter hits to be Silenced (destroyed and removed). BINARY board-state gate: the Volley can ONLY damage crystals in Dry bands — a crystal in a Brine-deep band AUTO-PASSES (the water cushions the glass), so any Shatter dice rolled against a wet crystal simply do nothing. A crystal that is already Set is immune. This is the mirror of the Set Hour: the attacker can only break what the defender can no longer seal, and vice versa — they fight a tug-of-war over the single band that flips each round.

specialRules.name: Collateral in the Crossfire (the custody dilemma)
specialRules.text: Whenever ANY shooting attack (from either side, at any target) MISSES while a model in the firing line is in or adjacent to an Exposed (Dry-band, Un-set) crystal's zone, the shooter immediately rolls those missed dice against that crystal: each natural 6 is a Shatter hit toward Silencing it. This applies to defenders too — a Mnemarch defending a crystal who fires near it can shatter the very thing they came to save. AUTO-PASS while wet: a crystal in a Brine-deep band ignores all collateral. Decision created every activation: take the shot near the prize and risk erasing it, or hold fire and let the enemy advance.

specialRules.name: Custody Carry (the Ignore-tradeoff)
specialRules.text: A model in base contact with a LOOSE crystal may pick it up and carry it (Held). A model carrying a Litany CANNOT Run and CANNOT shoot — it trades all mobility-rush and firepower for custody, an Ignore-X swap, not a stat penalty. While Held, a crystal cannot be Shattered by enemy fire (a body shields it) but ALSO cannot be Set (the Set Hour needs the crystal seated in its socket, base-contact with terrain, not in a hand). Use it to drag a shoreward crystal seaward into wet protection before its band dries — but you give up your gun to do it. Reliquiae cannot carry; only player models can.

specialRules.name: Re-dreaming the Drowned (the Grief engine, attacker-controlled)
specialRules.text: At the very start of each round, before the Toll, the ATTACKER must spend every token currently in the Grief pool: one token returns one set-aside Reliquia to the board in ANY Dry band (auto-return, no roll, attacker chooses placement). Reliquiae are slow horde models the attacker moves and may fire (they do not generate Breaking Volleys, only ordinary fire that can still cause Collateral shatters). A Reliquia in base contact with a crystal LOCKS it Grey: that crystal cannot be Sealed by a Chorister and, if it Shatters, scores for nobody and adds a token to Grief. A Reliquia standing in a Brine-deep band is safe; one the tide passes over and that ends a later round still in the now-Dry band is itself erased — set aside again, returning to the pool of re-dreamable bodies. Visible on/off tied entirely to the terrain overlay: wet = present, dry-and-passed = gone.

scenarios.name: The Last Liquidation
scenarios.hook: When the Long Toll reads four-of-six, the Brine-Factors call a Liquidation: one crystal, the Vault-Heart, holds a moment so old that no Choir has dared seal it and no Scour has dared shatter it — and now the tide that protected it is leaving. The Factors mean to carry it off the table and lock it in the Hold before the Sea goes dry, turning a holy hour into untouchable Coin. But Veyl's grief has already noticed the water going. As the brine recedes the drowned re-dream up out of the exposed pools, and the Sediment want only one thing: to drag the Vault-Heart back down into the receding water where no ledger can ever reach it. Everyone else has come to make sure that when the Toll strikes Dry, the crystal is in their hands and not the sea's — or, failing that, that it is in nobody's. A crystal taken is a memory owned forever. A crystal drowned is a memory that never stops happening. A crystal shattered is a memory that never was. Tonight only one of those three will be true.
scenarios.setup: Play on a 3 x 3 ft table. Lay 6-10 terrain pieces, then overlay a fixed Tide Track of 6 notches along one table edge where every player can see it. Divide the board into six numbered Tide Bands running parallel to the tideline (Band 1 nearest the dry shore, Band 6 nearest the deep). At the start, Bands 1-2 are Dry (dry side of the terrain overlay up) and Bands 3-6 are Brine-deep (wet side up). Place ONE special crystal model, the Vault-Heart, dead centre in Band 4 (Brine-deep, so it starts auto-protected and Loose). Place two ordinary Loose crystals, one each in Band 3 and Band 5. Set out a single shared Grief pool dish beside the Tide Track with a reserve of tokens. Each player nominates one Extraction Edge (their own table edge). Set the Tide marker on notch 1.
scenarios.deployment: Roll off. The winner picks a long table edge as their Extraction Edge; the loser takes the opposite. (In a 3-4 player game, each player takes a quarter and a corner Extraction Edge.) Players then alternate placing one model at a time within 6 inches of their own edge. NO model may be deployed in Band 4 or in any Brine-deep band adjacent to the Vault-Heart — everyone starts on the dry margins and must wade inward as the tide that guards the prize drains away. Scouts/infiltrators deploy last but may not be placed in a Brine-deep band. The Vault-Heart and the two ordinary crystals are placed during Setup, before any models.
scenarios.objectives: This is an extraction-and-denial mission, not a body count. Your goal is to fix the Custody fate of the Vault-Heart at the moment the Toll strikes Dry. Three mutually exclusive winning fates exist: EXTRACTED (a Held carrier walks it off your own Extraction Edge — it becomes Coin), DROWNED (a Held carrier spends its whole activation to shove the crystal one band deeper into a still-Brine-deep band and let go — it sinks beyond all custody), or SEALED (a ritual completes it in place in a wet band — Set forever). If the Vault-Heart is still Loose on the table when the Toll strikes Dry in its band it is Exposed to the swarm. Carrying it is an IGNORE tradeoff: a model in base contact may pick it up to become Held, but a Held model cannot Run (no second Move) and cannot Shoot — it trades speed and firepower for custody, exactly as a Litania-bearer does.
scenarios.victory: Score the instant the Toll strikes Dry (end of Round 6). Vault-Heart EXTRACTED off your Extraction Edge = 3 points to the carrying player. DROWNED into a Brine-deep band = 3 points to the drowning player. SEALED in a wet band by a completed ritual = 3 points to the sealing player. If the Vault-Heart is SHATTERED at any point it never happened and is worth 0 to everyone. Plus 1 point per ordinary crystal you Extracted, Drowned or Sealed, and 1 point if you control (more models within 3 inches than any rival) the band the Vault-Heart ends in. Most points wins. Ties broken in favour of the player holding the fewest Coin — the sea remembers hoarders last.
scenarios.length: 6 rounds (fixed by the Tide Track — the game ends the instant the Toll strikes Dry on notch 6; no turn-counting required, the water tells you the time).
scenarios.twist: THE WATER LEAVES THE TABLE. At the start of every round the Tide marker advances one mandatory, unskippable notch and ALL of one numbered Band flips from Brine-deep to Dry via the double-sided overlay: Round 2 flips Band 3, Round 3 flips Band 4 (the Vault-Heart's home — the hinge of the game), Round 4 flips Band 5, Round 5 flips Band 6, Round 6 the Toll strikes Dry and the game ends. The moment Band 4 goes Dry the Vault-Heart loses its water cushion: it becomes Exposed (Shatter-eligible) AND the Drown option dies for that band forever — you can only Drown into water that is still there, so after Round 3 a would-be Drowner must drag the unarmed, no-Run carrier toward the retreating deep while everyone shoots at it. Whoever owns the instant Band 4 flips owns whether the prize is sealed forever, sold forever, sunk forever, or silenced forever.

specialRules.name: The Long Toll (the audible clock)
specialRules.text: At the start of every round, advance the Tide marker one notch — mandatory, unskippable, identical for all players. Each notch flips its pre-defined Band from Brine-deep to Dry by turning the terrain overlay (wet side down, dry side up). BINARY and instant: a band is wet or dry, never partial. Any crystal in a Dry band is Exposed. When the marker reaches notch 6 the Toll strikes Dry and the game ends immediately — score the Verdict.

specialRules.name: Custody & Collateral (the Sixes shatter)
specialRules.text: Crystals have a Custody state: Loose, Held (a model in base contact controls it), or Set. Whenever a Shoot or Fight MISSES a target standing in or adjacent to an Exposed crystal's band, roll those missed dice against the crystal: each natural 6 is a Shatter (no modifiers, raw dice). Three Shatters and the crystal is removed — it never happened, nobody scores it. A crystal in a Brine-deep band AUTO-PASSES every shatter check (water cushions the glass); the instant its band flips Dry on the Toll, that protection is gone. BINARY decision every activation: take the risky shot near the prize, or hold fire.

specialRules.name: The Liquidator's Grip (carry = IGNORE-X)
specialRules.text: A model in base contact with a Loose crystal may, as one action, pick it up: it becomes Held. A Held carrier IGNORES its own Run and Shoot — it may take a single Move and may Fight, nothing more, until it drops the crystal (a free action) or is removed (the crystal falls Loose where it stood). This is the whole tradeoff: custody costs you mobility and guns. A Held Vault-Heart is the only crystal that can be Extracted, Drowned, or fed to the Sealing ritual.

specialRules.name: Drown the Ledger (the Sediment denial)
specialRules.text: A Held carrier standing at the edge of a still Brine-deep band may spend its ENTIRE activation to Drown the crystal: shove it one band deeper into the water and let go. The crystal is gone — beyond Coin, beyond Choir, beyond Scour — and scores for the drowning player as DROWNED. You can only Drown into a band that is currently wet, so the receding Toll closes this option one band at a time. AUTO-RESOLVES, no roll: the only question is whether you can reach live water with a no-Run carrier before the deep retreats out of reach.

specialRules.name: The Dreaming Grief (re-dreaming swarm)
specialRules.text: The shared Grief pool gains one token every time ANY crystal Shatters and one token every time the Toll flips a band to Dry (board-wide — all factions trigger it). At the start of each round, before activations, spend 2 Grief tokens to Re-dream one set-aside Reliquia back onto the board in any Dry band — AUTO-RETURN, no roll. Reliquiae removed as casualties are set aside, not destroyed. A Reliquia caught in a band when it flips Dry is fine the first time; one the tide passes over a SECOND time is erased for good. The more the others shatter and the drier it gets, the larger the swarm that smothers the prize.

specialRules.name: The Sealing Choir (the in-place ritual)
specialRules.text: A Mnemarch-aligned model in base contact with the Held Vault-Heart in a Brine-deep band may, instead of acting normally, add a Sealing die to the ritual: roll one die, and a natural 6 places one Seal on the crystal. Three Seals and the Vault-Heart is Set — permanent, SEALED, scored, and worthless to every Factor and Sediment forever. The ritual AUTO-FAILS in a Dry band (the choir needs the water's resonance), so the Toll is a closing window: every band that flips dry strips one more place the Choir could ever finish. Extra models in contact each add their own Sealing die — bring the choir, beat the clock.

scenarios.name: The Undertow Verdict
scenarios.hook: This is the deepest receding the Litany Sea has ever dared: a spring ebb that bares the drowned cathedral floor in three falling stages, and with it the worst of Veyl's dreaming grief. The Ash Iconoclasts came to silence the cathedral for good. The Sediment came because the Iconoclasts came, drawn to the wake of breaking the way undertow is drawn to a wreck. Between them the Mnemarchs race to Set the holy moments before the silence falls, and the Brine-Factors race to Liquidate them before the silence makes them worthless. But the Sea is not finished remembering. Every crystal shattered, every zone left dry, swells a tide that turns and comes surging back, and what that undertow drags under it counts twice. By the final Toll, nobody is fighting over the prize they came for. Three stages, three Verdicts, one receding clock no faction can slow.
scenarios.setup: Play on a 4x4 board divided into a 6x6 zone grid: the drowned cathedral floor. Lay the double-sided wet/dry overlays so the central 3x4 block of zones (the nave) begins Brine-deep, and the surrounding aisle ring begins Dry. Place 8 crystals, the Litany of the cathedral: 5 in the wet nave, 3 scattered loose across the dry aisles. Set a Tide Track of 6 notches, and mark notches 2 and 4 with a colored band: these are the two STAGE BREAKS. Pre-define the dry-flip bands so the nave recedes from the OUTSIDE IN: the aisle-facing nave zones flip first (notches 1 and 2), the deep center flips last (notches 5 and 6), the inverse of an ordinary ebb. The Grief pool starts at zero. Place a Hold box off the Brine-Factors' edge, and lay an Undertow Track (a separate row of 6 empty slots) beside the Tide Track.
scenarios.deployment: Diagonal deployment. The Ash Iconoclasts and the Sediment deploy in OPPOSITE corners, each confined to a 10-inch quadrant: they are the axis of this fight and must stare across the whole board at each other. The Mnemarchs and the Brine-Factors deploy along the two remaining board edges, within 6 inches of their edge. No model may begin in a Brine-deep zone (you cannot start standing in the Sea). After deployment, whichever faction has the FEWEST models on the board takes the first activation: the underdog reads the water first.
scenarios.objectives: Scoring changes by stage, and the Toll decides the stage. A crystal can only ever be claimed ONCE, by the first method that fully resolves on it. STAGE ONE (rounds 1-2, the Choir's Hour): only SET crystals (Mnemarchs) and LIQUIDATED crystals taken into Hold (Brine-Factors) score. These are wet-side acts. STAGE TWO (rounds 3-4, the Breaking Hour): only SHATTERED crystals (Ash Iconoclasts) and DROWNED crystals re-covered into play (Sediment) score. These are dry-side acts; Setting and Liquidating still physically happen but bank zero points this stage. STAGE THREE (rounds 5-6, the Undertow): ALL four methods score again, and every crystal whose fate is recorded on the Undertow Track scores DOUBLE for whoever last controlled it.

specialRules.name: The Long Toll (three falling stages)
specialRules.text: At the start of every round, advance the Tide marker one notch and flip that notch's pre-defined band of nave zones from Brine-deep to Dry, outside-in, BINARY and instant. Each band that flips drops one token into the Grief pool. Crossing a STAGE BREAK notch (2 to 3, and 4 to 5) immediately swaps which scoring methods are live: no bookkeeping, the marker's position on the track IS the rulebook. When the marker reaches the final notch the Toll strikes Dry, the third Verdict scores, and the game ends. No counting rounds in your head: the water leaving the table tells you the stage and the time left.

specialRules.name: The Undertow (erasure as a resource)
specialRules.text: Every time ANY crystal Shatters, place a marker in the next empty slot of the Undertow Track. The instant the Undertow Track fills the slots for the current stage, the tide TURNS: at the start of the next round, instead of the normal flip, the most-recently-dried band flips BACK to Brine-deep for one round (the water surges over the wreck). Crystals re-covered this way AUTO-PASS shatter checks again while wet, and any Reliquia that band would have erased is spared. This is the only force on the table that moves water backward, and ONLY Shattering builds it: the Iconoclasts dig the swarm's shelter with their own volleys.

specialRules.name: Symbiosis of Ash and Silt
specialRules.text: Custody and Collateral runs as written: an attack whose shots MISS a target in or adjacent to an Exposed crystal's zone rolls those misses against the crystal, and each natural 6 is a Shatter hit (no modifiers, raw dice); Brine-deep zones AUTO-PASS, water cushions the glass. Here every Shatter does double work and drops TWO Grief tokens (one for the break, one for the silence). At the start of each round, spend Grief one-for-one to Re-dream set-aside Reliquiae back onto any Dry zone, AUTO-RETURN, no roll. The more the Iconoclasts break, the larger the horde the Sediment re-dream into the exact zones the breaking just cleared. IGNORE only while wet: a Reliquia the receding tide leaves Dry and then the tide passes over a SECOND time is erased and set aside.

specialRules.name: Banked, Not Lost (carrying and cross-stage acts)
specialRules.text: A model carrying a crystal (a Litany) cannot Run and cannot shoot, an IGNORE-X trade of mobility and firepower for custody. Acts taken in the wrong stage are not wasted, they are LOADED: a crystal Set during the Breaking Hour holds its claim but pays nothing until the Undertow; a crystal carried but not yet Liquidated when a Stage Break falls keeps its carrier's grip. BINARY: a crystal is claimed or unclaimed, and the first method to fully resolve locks it forever. This lets a faction plant during a stage that pays its enemy, betting the clock turns back in its favor before the final Toll.

scenarios.twist: At the second Stage Break (the start of round 5, the Undertow proper), the deepest nave zones, the last wet ground and the safest crystals all game, begin to dry from the CENTER OUTWARD, reversing every prior tide. The crystals everyone treated as untouchable vault stock are Exposed all at once, while the aisle crystals the tide first abandoned may already lie sheltered under a turned Undertow. Every faction's safe holdings and risky holdings trade places in a single Toll, the Mnemarchs' sealed deep-nave Litanies are suddenly Shatter-eligible, and the Verdict that doubles is the one nobody planned to fight.
scenarios.length: 6 rounds (one per tide), resolved in three two-round stages.
scenarios.victory: Three Verdicts are scored, at the end of round 2, round 4, and round 6, and points accumulate across all three. The faction with the most total scored crystals when the Toll strikes Dry wins the Undertow Verdict, counting Undertow-doubled crystals at their doubled value. Ties break first to crystals scored during the Undertow stage, then to the number of Shatters that fed the turning tide, so the Iconoclasts and the Sediment, fittingly, settle their own grudge last.

campaign.name: The Tide of Remembrance
campaign.overview: The Litany Sea does not forget. Every blow struck on its salt-bleached shores is recited back by the tide, and warbands that fight across the campaign are slowly rewritten by what the Sea remembers of them. The Tide of Remembrance is a persistent campaign for two or more players, each commanding a warband that carries its history from one battle to the next. You begin with a 100-point warband and a blank Litany — a roster sheet on which every name, every wound, and every deed is recorded. As the campaign runs, your fighters earn places in the Litany: they become Remembered, they take scars the Sea will not let them lose, and they harden into veterans whose reputations precede them onto the next beach. The factions fight not for ground alone but for the right to author what the Sea recalls: the Mnemarchs to fix the hours in their proper order, the Ash Iconoclasts to burn the record clean, the Brine-Factors to price and sell every memory at the Salt Exchange, and the Sediment to drown the waking world in older, deeper dreams. A warband is never just a warband here — it is a verse the Sea is still composing.
campaign.howItWorks: Battles are strung together by the Litany — your warband's living record — and by the Tide, a shared campaign clock. Play any scenario from the rulebook. Before each game, both players bring their warband's current Litany and every advancement and scar already earned; nothing resets between games. After the game, resolve three steps in order. First, the WINNER adds one Verse to their Litany: a line naming the battle, the beach, and one fighter who distinguished themselves — that named fighter immediately rolls once on the Advancement track below. Second, every model REMOVED from play during the game, on either side, rolls once on the Battle-Scars table to learn what the Sea kept of it; a model with no scars left to gain simply walks away Remembered. Third, the Tide turns: move the shared Tide marker on one, then the player holding the FEWEST Recited Beaches picks the next scenario and table edge, so a player who is losing is never starved of choices. A short campaign is one Tide of six battles; a full campaign is three Tides (eighteen battles), after which the warband with the most Verses in its Litany has written itself deepest into the Sea and wins. The golden rule: everything a model earns is a named, binary entry on the roster — a keyword it has or does not have. You never tally running bonuses, and no advancement ever changes a target number on the way to the same result.

progression.name: The Litany (warband roster)
progression.text: Your warband sheet is its Litany. List each model by name, its faction, and any keywords it has earned (Remembered, plus any scars). The Litany is the single source of truth between games — if it is not written on the Litany, it does not carry over. Keep it simple: a name and a short list of words after it, never a column of plus-and-minus numbers.

progression.name: Earning a Verse
progression.text: After a win, name one surviving fighter who turned the battle. That fighter is the Verse-bearer for this game and rolls once on the Advancement Roll. A model may bear many Verses across a campaign but rolls only once per game it is named, so spread the glory or concentrate it — your choice shapes whether you build one legend or a balanced band.

progression.name: Advancement Roll (D6)
progression.text: When a fighter advances, roll a D6 and apply the matching gift. Each is a clean on/off ability, never a stacking number. 1-2 Quick Study: this model gains the Remembered keyword (if it already has it, re-roll). 3 Sea-Sure Hand: once per game, this model may re-roll all of its missed hits from a single Shoot or Fight. 4 Unforgetting Eye: once per game, this model's Shoot or Fight ignores Cover entirely. 5 Carried by the Tide: once per game, this model may auto-pass a single Nerve roll instead of rolling. 6 Named Aloud: choose any one of results 3, 4, or 5 — the Sea has spoken your fighter's name plainly.

progression.name: Remembered (the veteran keyword)
progression.text: A fighter the Sea has fixed in its memory gains the Remembered keyword. A Remembered model rolls one extra die the first time each game it Shoots or Fights — a single burst of recalled prowess, declared before you roll, used once and gone. Remembered is binary: a model either is or is not, and the extra die never stacks with a second Remembered. It is the backbone of veterancy — visible on the table the moment that fighter first acts.

progression.name: Litany of the Fallen
progression.text: When a named, Remembered fighter is finally removed for good (a Battle-Scars result that kills them), do not erase the line — strike it through and keep it. Once per campaign per struck-through name, when any friendly model is within 6" of where a Fallen comrade died on the board, that friendly model may auto-pass one Nerve roll. The dead still steady the living. This is declared and spent the instant it triggers, tied to a spot you can point to on the table.

progression.name: Leader's Litany
progression.text: Your Leader keeps the warband's Litany and may, once per game, re-narrate a single moment: re-roll one die just rolled by any friendly model within 6" of the Leader (the original Command ability still works as printed). If your Leader is ever removed for good, the next game a surviving Remembered model is promoted and inherits this rule — the Litany passes to a new keeper, and the war goes on.

progression.name: Spending Verses (between Tides)
progression.text: At the end of each Tide, you may spend Verses to recruit. Each unspent Verse lets you add one new rank-and-file model to your warband from your faction list at no points cost, written fresh onto the Litany with no keywords. This keeps a battered warband alive without bookkeeping: a Verse is a single recruit, full stop. You never convert Verses into points or partial upgrades.

campaign.territories: The map is the Litany Sea's retreating tide-line: a chain of named beaches the Sea recites at low water and swallows again at high. Sketch or print a row of seven to nine Beaches between the players — for example the Set-Hour Strand, the Cinder Shoals, the Salt Exchange, the Re-Dreaming Flats, the Drowned Vault, the Glass Reef, and the Mouth. Each Beach grants a single, binary boon to whoever holds it, never a number to add up. Win a battle fought on or for a Beach and you Recite it: place your token there; it is yours until someone takes it from you in a later battle. A held Beach gives its keeper one of these on/off perks for any game they fight FROM it: the Salt Exchange lets one model per game re-roll its Advancement Roll if it earns one; the Drowned Vault lets the holder field one extra Remembered model's bonus die from reserve once per game; the Set-Hour Strand lets the holder choose to go first in Round 1 without rolling Initiative; the Re-Dreaming Flats let one removed friendly model return to the board edge once per campaign. The Mouth is the central, contested Beach: whoever holds it at the end of each Tide earns a free Verse. Players spread thin across many Beaches gain many small boons but defend a long line; players who clench a few key Beaches concentrate their power. Holdings are tracked by tokens on the map — visible, binary, and instantly read at a glance.

injuries.result: Taken by the Tide. The Sea keeps this fighter for good — remove the model from your Litany permanently (strike the name through; it may still steady the living via Litany of the Fallen). If this would remove your Leader, the Litany passes to a surviving Remembered model next game instead.

Salt in the Wound. The brine got into the hurt and would not leave. This model misses the NEXT battle entirely (resting in the surf), then returns with no lasting harm. Note it on the Litany; cross it off once the battle is sat out.

Rust-Lung. The damp recitation of the Sea fills this fighter's chest. This model gains the Rust-Lung keyword: while Broken, it is Shaken on a Nerve roll of 1-3 instead of 1-2. A clean threshold change, never a running penalty — it either has Rust-Lung or it does not.

Hollowed Eye. A shard of glass-reef cost this fighter half its sight. This model gains the Hollowed Eye keyword: it may no longer benefit from the Aim action's Cover-ignoring (it can still Aim to re-roll a miss). Binary and instant — Aim simply stops piercing Cover for this one model.

Scar-Litany. The wound healed into a story the Sea loves to tell. This model gains the Remembered keyword (if it already has it, treat this result as a 6). The fighter walks away harder than before, its name now sung at low tide.

Named by the Sea. The Sea spoke this fighter's name aloud as it fell, and would not let it die. The model survives with no harm AND its warband immediately adds one Verse to its Litany — a dying breath that wrote itself into memory. If the model already has Remembered, the Verse is the whole reward.

terrainTypes.name: Brine-deep (wet overlay)
terrainTypes.text: A zone showing its WET side. Models and crystals here are submerged to the chest. AUTO-PASS: any crystal in a Brine-deep zone automatically passes every Shatter check — the water cushions the glass, so you can fire freely near a submerged Litany. Reliquiae standing here are NEVER erased while the zone is wet, regardless of how many times the Tide has been read. Movement cost: a model that ENTERS a Brine-deep zone cannot Run that activation (the drag of the water) — this is a binary on/off restriction, not a penalty to its move stat. When the Toll flips this overlay to its Dry side, every protection above ends instantly and simultaneously for everything standing in it.

terrainTypes.name: Dry Flats (dry overlay)
terrainTypes.text: A zone showing its DRY side, exposed by the receding Sea. Every crystal here is Exposed and therefore Shatter-eligible — missed shots in or adjacent to this zone roll for Shatter (natural 6s only). This is the only terrain where Reliquiae can be Re-dreamed onto the board from the Grief pool. A Reliquia that the Tide has passed over TWICE while standing on Dry Flats (i.e. it was already on a dried zone at the start of a round and is still there at the next Toll) is erased and removed — set the model fully aside, it does not return. Dry Flats offer no cover and no cushion: this is open, dangerous ground that did not exist last round.

terrainTypes.name: Crystal Shoals
terrainTypes.text: A specific Dry-only feature that appears where a dense seam of Litanies is exposed. Treat as Dry Flats for all Shatter and Re-dream purposes, PLUS: any model in base contact with a Crystal Shoal may attempt to Set a Loose crystal here (see Setting, optional rules) and a Held crystal carried INTO a Shoal counts as Set the instant the carrier ends an activation there. Crystal Shoals can never be flipped back to wet — once a Shoal is exposed it stays exposed for the rest of the game, a permanent landmark on the drying board.

terrainTypes.name: The Reliquary Pools
terrainTypes.text: Deep pockets that recede LAST. Mark two zones on the track as Reliquary Pools; their overlay only flips on the final two notches of the Tide. While still wet, a Reliquary Pool grants its AUTO-PASS shatter protection AND lets a model that begins its activation there make a single re-roll of all failed Shatter-avoidance is not needed (crystals auto-pass) — instead the carrier may RE-ROLL one failed hit when shooting OUT of the pool, the clear water steadying the aim. A binary perk tied to standing in the last water on the table; it vanishes the moment the pool dries.

terrainTypes.name: Salt-Crust Ridges
terrainTypes.text: Raised dry ground that the brine never covered. Always Dry, never flips. A model fully behind a Salt-Crust Ridge IGNORES the first hit it would suffer each round (the crust takes the shot) — binary, once per round, no tracking of damage values. Crystals cannot exist on a Ridge (nothing fragile survived up here), so Ridges are pure firing positions: safe to shoot FROM, with no Shatter risk created by your own missed shots originating here, though misses can still land on crystals in the Dry zone you are shooting INTO.

environmentEvents.name: The Toll Strikes True
environmentEvents.text: The receding water shrieks across the salt. Every model standing in a zone that flipped to Dry THIS round must immediately pass a single die (natural 6 = caught footing, stays) or be displaced into the nearest still-wet zone; if none is adjacent, the model goes Prone where it stands. No modifiers — one raw die, binary outcome. Crystals do not move. This makes the freshly-dried band a moment of chaos every time the Sea pulls back.

environmentEvents.name: Grief Flinches
environmentEvents.text: Veyl re-remembers a face. Add one extra token to the Grief pool beyond any gained from shatters/dryings this round. Then, if the Grief pool holds 6 or more tokens, one set-aside Reliquia AUTO-RETURNS to a Dry zone of the active player's choice for free (does not spend tokens). The horde lurches forward precisely because the board is degrading — a visible threat that scales with the pool, not a hidden timer.

environmentEvents.name: Glass Sings
environmentEvents.text: The Exposed crystals resonate. Until the next Toll, every Shatter check across the board is rolled with one EXTRA die per crystal (still only natural 6s count as Shatter hits). A binary danger window: this round, shooting near any Exposed crystal is markedly more likely to break it. Players who want intact history hold fire; players who want to deny it to others let the shots fly. Brine-deep crystals still AUTO-PASS and ignore this entirely.

environmentEvents.name: Low Tide Clarity
environmentEvents.text: For one round the air over the dry flats goes glass-clear. Every model may RE-ROLL one failed hit when shooting at a target standing in a Dry zone. No bonus to anything in the water — the clarity only helps you hit what the Sea has abandoned. A clean re-roll, applied instantly, that rewards committing to the exposed ground.

environmentEvents.name: The Salt-Dead Stir
environmentEvents.text: Reliquiae remember they are owed. Every Reliquia currently on the board may, this round, make a free 'reach' — it counts as being in base contact for Custody purposes with any Loose crystal in its own zone, allowing the horde to seize a Litany without a normal activation. Binary: in-zone Loose crystals can be claimed by the swarm now. The other factions must decide whether to clear the zone or concede the relic to the dead.

environmentEvents.name: A Pool Closes Forever
environmentEvents.text: The Sea makes a decision. Immediately flip ONE additional Brine-deep zone to its Dry side, chosen by the player whose faction is currently scoring lowest (the world turns against the leader). This is an off-schedule drying: it triggers all the usual consequences at once — crystals there become Exposed, a Grief token is added, and any Reliquia the tide has now passed over twice is erased. The Long Toll has skipped a breath; the clock just got louder.

optionalRules.name: Setting the Litany (permanent custody)
optionalRules.text: A model in base contact with a Loose or Held crystal on a Crystal Shoal may spend its full activation to SET it: roll one die, natural 6 = the crystal becomes Set (permanent custody, scored at the Verdict for whoever Set it, can never be Shattered or Re-claimed). Anything other than a 6, the crystal stays Loose/Held and the activation is spent. No partial progress, no accumulating counters — each attempt is one raw die, all-or-nothing. Setting is the only way to make a relic truly safe before the Sea dries; it locks your history in but costs you a whole activation under fire.

optionalRules.name: The Carrier's Burden (IGNORE-X custody)
optionalRules.text: A model carrying a Held crystal embodies the central tradeoff in full: it cannot Run and cannot Shoot (a strict binary IGNORE of both abilities), trading all mobility-beyond-walk and all firepower for custody. In exchange, a carrier AUTO-PASSES any Shatter check caused by enemy fire passing through its own zone — it shields the Litany with its body. If the carrier is removed as a casualty, the crystal drops Loose in its zone (it does NOT shatter from the fall). This rule makes seizing a relic a genuine commitment: the moment you pick it up you are a slow, silent, walking objective.

optionalRules.name: Re-dreaming Escalation (the horde engine)
optionalRules.text: Formalizes the Grief pool as a scaling swarm. At the start of each round, before any activation, the controlling player of the Reliquiae spends Grief tokens 1-for-1 to AUTO-RETURN set-aside Reliquiae into any Dry zone(s) — no rolls, no placement contest. Cap the table at the number of Reliquia models physically owned; excess Grief tokens stay banked for later rounds. Because every shatter and every drying feeds the pool board-wide, the other three factions literally build the horde that hunts them. Optional intensifier: if the Grief pool is ever 10+ at a Toll, all Re-dreamed Reliquiae that round may be placed in base contact with an enemy model rather than merely in a Dry zone — the dead arrive already reaching.

optionalRules.name: The Verdict (end-state scoring)
optionalRules.text: When the marker reaches the final notch and the Toll strikes Dry, the game ends immediately mid-action — finish no further activations. Score ONLY intact, controlled history: each Set crystal scores for its owner; each Held crystal scores for the faction whose model holds it; each Loose crystal in a faction's sole zone scores for that faction. Shattered crystals score for NO ONE — they never happened. Reliquiae score nothing but deny: any zone containing more Reliquiae than enemy models is Contested and its Loose crystals score for no faction. This makes the binary custody states the entire win condition: you win by what survived the Sea, not by what you destroyed.

optionalRules.name: Reading the Water (no hidden timers)
optionalRules.text: An enforcement rule for tournament/competitive play: NOTHING in the game may be tracked off-board. The Tide marker, the wet/dry overlays, the Custody states (Loose/Held/Set), and the Grief pool tokens are the complete game state — any disagreement is resolved by looking at the table, never at notes or memory. If an effect cannot be represented by moving the Tide marker, flipping an overlay, changing a crystal's physical custody, or adding/removing a Grief token, it is not legal. This keeps every faction reading the same living clock and guarantees the SIXES promise: instant to apply, tied to visible board state, no arithmetic between you and the result.

optionalRules.name: Twice-Passed Erasure Tracking (visible on/off)
optionalRules.text: To make erasure unmissable, place a single 'salt marker' on any Dry zone the instant it flips. At each subsequent Toll, any Reliquia still standing on a salt-marked zone is erased (the tide has passed it twice) and the salt marker is removed with it; fresh dryings get a new salt marker. Wet zones never carry a salt marker. A model can therefore see at a glance which dried ground is lethal to the horde next round, turning erasure into a positional resource: shove the dead onto salt-marked flats, or rescue your own by walking them into the last water.

prose.openingFiction:
The salt is up to your shins and falling.

You feel it leave — not drain, leave, the way a held breath leaves a body — and somewhere out across the flat a pool finishes drying and rings like a struck bell that has decided to keep ringing. That note is a moment going hard. Someone is being born in it, or buried in it, forever, because no one was standing close enough to stop it.

Ahead of you the crystal you came three tides to take sits in its shallow socket, no bigger than a child's fist, holding inside its facets a single afternoon that an entire order would die to keep and another would die to break. It is humming. Everything here hums. The dead are standing up again where the water let them go, salt-jawed, re-remembering how to walk, and the rust sun has not moved, will not move, has forgotten the courtesy of setting.

You wade. You do not run — running makes a wake, and a wake is a hammer, and the thing you want is glass. Behind you a rival shouts a price. Ahead, a zealot lifts a mallet to the sky.

Between you and the tear: forty steps of evaporating god.

Take it whole. Take it humming. The Sea is counting, and it is almost done.
prose.worldIntro:
THE LITANY SEA is a game about stealing the past before it stops being negotiable.

A god named Veyl was struck down in the deep of years, and where it fell it did not bleed — it wept, and its weeping filled the basin of the world. That ocean of grief is the Litany Sea, and every drop of its brine is a remembered moment. But the Sea is drying. The rust-red sun has not set in living memory; the water recedes thigh-deep, then ankle-deep, then gone, and where it goes it crystallizes — salt-glass, hard and humming, each shard a fossilized instant you can re-live, sell, edit, set forever, or shatter so it never happened at all.

You play a memory-archivist of one of four rival orders, wading a flat that is audibly counting down. You do not fight for ground. You do not fight for kills. You fight for custody of specific, fragile, irreplaceable crystals — and the cruelty of every battle is that the thing you came to win is the easiest thing on the board to break. When the last pool dries, whichever version of the past is still crystallized becomes the only past there ever was.

The dead rise where the tide abandons them. The crystals ring as they crack. You have one long afternoon.

Tone: a sacred heist played at low tide on a dying mind — reverent, grief-soaked, and tolling like a bell that knows the hour.

grandTimeline.when: The Deep Past — The First Weeping
grandTimeline.event: Veyl, the leviathan-deity, is struck down by hands no surviving crystal remembers. It does not die and it does not bleed. It begins to weep, and its grief floods the basin of the world. The Litany Sea is born — an ocean in which every drop holds a moment the god is still feeling.

grandTimeline.when: The Long Tides — The Age of Brine
grandTimeline.event: Generations live on and beneath the Sea believing it to be the corpse-water of a slain god. The brine is fathomless and full. The dead stay drowned. No one yet understands that the Sea is not a grave but a wound, and that the moments suspended in it are not the god's history but its present — a life being re-felt, slowly, in the dark.

The waters begin to drop. Pools dry and crystallize for the first time; the first salt-glass forms and the first moment is accidentally set forever by villagers who only meant to gather salt. The rust sun rises that morning and does not set. It has not set since. The Toll begins.

Four readings of the drying split the survivors. The Mnemarchs vow to FIX the past and enshrine it. The Ash Iconoclasts vow to SHATTER it and free the god from memory. The Brine-Factors open the Salt Exchange to SELL it. The Sediment — the salt-dead and their grief-touched shepherds — rise to FREE it back into the Sea. The wars for custody begin.

The flat becomes a battlefield where no one digs in and no one body-counts. Orders wade for named, fragile crystals, and learn the central agony of the Sea: that you cannot win the moment you came for without risking shattering it in the crossfire. Whole histories are lost not to the enemy but to a single misplaced wake.

As the Sea thins, the dead of forgotten moments begin standing up wherever the tide retreats — the Reliquiae, salt-bodied and re-remembering. The Sediment grows stronger as the board dies. The truth dawns on the few who can bear it: the rising dead are the god flinching at memories it cannot release. Veyl is not dead. Veyl is grieving, and almost finished.

grandTimeline.when: The Present — The Sixth Toll, Low Tide
grandTimeline.event: The Sea is thigh-deep and falling fast. By every reckoning it has a single long afternoon left. The five great reckonings unfold across the drying flat as the orders converge on the last crystals in the last pools, each racing to be the version of the past still standing when the brine runs out.

grandTimeline.when: The Hour Yet to Strike — The Toll Strikes Dry
grandTimeline.event: When the final pool crystallizes, Veyl finishes the thought. Whichever order's past is set at that instant authors the single memory the god carries into death — and becomes the only true history of the world. Every other past does not lose. It ceases ever to have happened, taking its winners and its dead and its very having-been with it.

sectionEpigraphs.quote: Do not call it salvage. We are not robbing a god. We are arguing with one, and the brine is running out of patience faster than we are running out of argument.
sectionEpigraphs.attribution: Hierophant Calveth of the Sediment, last sermon at ankle-depth

sectionEpigraphs.quote: A kill costs you nothing here. A wake costs you everything. Wade as though the water were sleeping — because it is, and it dreams of you.
sectionEpigraphs.attribution: First Lesson of the Wading, Mnemarch catechism

sectionEpigraphs.quote: You may take the crystal whole or you may take it shattered, but the god only keeps the whole one — and so do we.
sectionEpigraphs.attribution: Custodian-Sergeant Orrin, on the rules of seizure

sectionEpigraphs.quote: Every shard is a lie that holds a soul in place. Mercy is the mallet. We did not come to read the past. We came to let it stop screaming.
sectionEpigraphs.attribution: Pyre-Speaker of the Ash Iconoclasts, the Unwriting Rite

sectionEpigraphs.quote: Truth is a price, friend. Name yours. I have a Tuesday in here that three orders swear never happened — going cheap, going fast, going once.
sectionEpigraphs.attribution: Factor Mireh of the Salt Exchange, working the low-tide floor

sectionEpigraphs.quote: They rise because the god flinches. You are not fighting corpses. You are fighting the parts of a mind that cannot let go — and neither, I think, can you.
sectionEpigraphs.attribution: Marginalia found set in a cracked Reliquiae crystal, author unknown

sectionEpigraphs.quote: Six tolls I have counted. The sixth is the one that does not stop. When the ringing goes steady, the afternoon is spent, and so is everyone who is still wrong.
sectionEpigraphs.attribution: The Drying Almanac, attributed to the last Tidewarden

sectionEpigraphs.quote: Win and you are remembered. Lose and you were never here at all — not your banner, not your dead, not the hand that turned these very pages.
sectionEpigraphs.attribution: Inscription over the threshold of the Set Hour

prose.closingFiction:
The last pool is the size of a coin now, and it is bright, and it is singing the highest note the Sea has ever held.

Around it the four orders have gone still. There is nothing left to seize. There is only the watching, and the water leaving one drop at a time, and the crystal you set or shattered or sold ringing steady in your fist — already the only version, already true, already the thought the god is about to finish.

The rust sun, at long last, leans toward the horizon. It remembers how to set. That is how you know.

When the coin of brine dries, Veyl draws its grief in like a final breath, and chooses — without choosing — the one moment it will carry down into the dark it was struck toward so long ago.

If that moment is yours, you are the world.

If it is not, then there was never a you to read this, never a Sea, never a god.

Only salt. Only the silence after a bell.

Listen. The ringing is steadying.
